meta.scope: IPF only. Evidence from other fibrotic diseases appears only where it is labelled indirect evidence.
meta.source_of_truth: the corrected Phase 0-6 research record; later corrections supersede earlier statements
meta.research_status: research cycle complete through Phase 6; no research lead promoted
meta.disclaimer: This is a research record, not medical advice. It grades published evidence and names what is missing. Nothing here establishes that a treatment is effective, safe or appropriate for any patient. Treatment decisions belong to a qualified clinician with the full patient context.
reading_rules: Slowing the rate of lung-function decline is not preserving lung function, not recovering lost function, not reversing fibrosis and not a cure.
A lung-function effect is not a demonstrated survival benefit. No drug in this record has randomised evidence of prolonging survival.
Patient-level prognostic association between lung-function decline and death does not establish that a treatment-induced change in decline predicts survival.
Poorly studied is not ineffective: it means the evidence needed to judge the intervention does not exist.
Missing, unretrieved or inaccessible evidence is not therapeutic promise.
A registry posting without an analysable between-arm result is identifiable as such and is not graded as published evidence.
A candidate held at verification is neither promoted nor rejected.
Every verdict is graded on one named outcome dimension only and carries its caveat.

map.statement: 48 development programmes in this record stopped before establishing a result. Their failure domain is the absence of an answer, not a negative answer: recruitment or operational failure (11), unknown reason (10), regulatory or commercial decision (9), safety or toxicity (7), stated futility (4) and trial design (3).
map.subject: 48 stopped programmes
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Unknown (no result was established; classification is of the stated stopping reason, not of efficacy)
map.caveat: A programme that stopped without a result is not evidence of either efficacy or inefficacy. It must not be read as a positive signal.
map.provenance: ipf_phase2_negative_results_register.csv (failure_domain='development stopped before a result was established')

map.statement: Eight investigational agents have a positive randomised signal in IPF that has not been tested at phase 3: AP01 (inhaled pirfenidone), BMS-986020, GSK3008348, LTI-03, TRK-250, bexotegrast, omipalisib and taladegib. Each rests on one small randomised trial.
map.subject: AP01; BMS-986020; GSK3008348; LTI-03; TRK-250; bexotegrast; omipalisib; taladegib
map.outcome_dimension: mostly rate of FVC decline (E1) or biomarker endpoints
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (one small randomised trial each; below the size and duration at which IPF nulls become decisive) (tier inherited from Phase 2)
map.caveat: Uncertain means one direction is indicated but the evidence cannot carry the claim. It is not a weak positive.

map.statement: Deupirfenidone is positive on a 26-week FVC endpoint in one phase 2b trial (ELEVATE-IPF), including against an active pirfenidone arm; no phase 3 result exists.
map.subject: deupirfenidone
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Probable (one randomised phase 2b trial, 26 weeks, Bayesian primary analysis) (tier inherited from Phase 2)
map.caveat: Uncertain means one direction is indicated but the evidence cannot carry the claim. It is not a weak positive.

map.statement: Admilparant's phase 2 IPF-cohort estimate has a confidence interval that includes zero; the statistically significant estimate comes from the separate progressive pulmonary fibrosis cohort of the same trial and is indirect evidence for IPF under scope limit L1.
map.subject: admilparant (BMS-986278)
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (IPF-cohort estimate not statistically significant; PPF-cohort result is indirect for IPF) (tier inherited from Phase 2)
map.caveat: Uncertain means one direction is indicated but the evidence cannot carry the claim. It is not a weak positive.

map.statement: Rentosertib (INS018_055) reported an exploratory FVC increase at its highest dose in a phase 2a trial whose primary endpoint was tolerability. The efficacy signal is not a tested hypothesis.
map.subject: INS018_055
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Hypothesis (primary endpoint was safety; efficacy exploratory, single dose group, n=18) (tier inherited from Phase 2)
map.caveat: Uncertain means one direction is indicated but the evidence cannot carry the claim. It is not a weak positive.

map.statement: Eight agents were null in IPF trials that were too small or too short for the null to be decisive: GLPG1205, azithromycin, cromolyn sodium (RVT-1601), etanercept, imatinib, inhaled carbon monoxide, macitentan and tralokinumab. These are unresolved, not refuted. Cromolyn sodium was removed from this statement in Phase 4: a phase 2b trial with a null primary cough endpoint exists (see M2.14).
map.subject: GLPG1205; azithromycin; etanercept; imatinib; inhaled carbon monoxide; macitentan; tralokinumab
map.outcome_dimension: various; mostly FVC (E1) or progression composites
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (null but underpowered; distinguished from the Failed class by trial size and phase) (tier inherited from Phase 2)
map.caveat: Uncertain means one direction is indicated but the evidence cannot carry the claim. It is not a weak positive.

map.statement: Six repurposed approved drugs have IPF evidence that cannot carry a conclusion: omeprazole, salbutamol, sirolimus and valganciclovir have small positive randomised results; losartan has non-randomised evidence only; metformin has observational evidence that is null. Phase 4 correction: for salbutamol, sirolimus, valganciclovir and omipalisib the trial's primary endpoint was not a clinical outcome, and the omeprazole cough interval includes no effect while lung-function differences in the same trial favour placebo.
map.subject: omeprazole; salbutamol; sirolimus; valganciclovir; losartan; metformin
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (small randomised or observational evidence; no adequately sized randomised test) (tier inherited from Phase 2)
map.caveat: Uncertain means one direction is indicated but the evidence cannot carry the claim. It is not a weak positive.

map.statement: Cell therapies and blood-derived biologics in IPF rest on non-randomised or very small randomised human evidence: mesenchymal stem cells, RegenD001, IW001, PBI-4050 and intravenous immunoglobulin.
map.subject: mesenchymal stem cells; RegenD001; IW001; PBI-4050; intravenous immunoglobulin
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (predominantly single-arm or open-label evidence; no controlled efficacy test) (tier inherited from Phase 2)
map.caveat: Uncertain means one direction is indicated but the evidence cannot carry the claim. It is not a weak positive.

map.statement: Symptomatic and supportive interventions other than nalbuphine and rehabilitation are unresolved: low-dose morphine and thalidomide each rest on one very small short crossover trial in cough; supplemental oxygen shows acute exercise benefit without long-term IPF-specific evidence; palliative care, CPAP, neuromuscular electrical stimulation and inspiratory muscle training have small or indirect evidence.
map.subject: morphine; thalidomide; oxygen; palliative care; continuous positive airway pressure; neuromuscular electrical stimulation; inspiratory muscle training
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (small, short, or ILD-wide rather than IPF-exclusive evidence) (tier inherited from Phase 2)
map.caveat: Uncertain means one direction is indicated but the evidence cannot carry the claim. It is not a weak positive.

map.statement: Seven named traditional-medicine interventions have randomised IPF-only trials that pass the prespecified screen (Jinbei oral liquid, Kangxian Huanji Granule, Qizhukangxian granules, Feiwei granules, umbilical moxibustion, Pulmonary Daoyin, Baduanjin exercise), and pooled syntheses of Chinese herbal medicine report benefit. Every such row is capped at Uncertain because risk of bias was only assessable from abstracts, samples are small, follow-up is short, and Chinese-language databases were not searched. Feiwei granules is author-reported null.
map.subject: Jinbei oral liquid (12-herb TCM compound); Kangxian Huanji Granule; Qizhukangxian granules; Feiwei granules; umbilical moxibustion; Pulmonary Daoyin (TCM rehabilitation programme); Baduanjin exercise; Chinese herbal medicine
map.outcome_dimension: lung function, symptoms, exercise capacity - varies by trial
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (capped by Phase 2 brief section 4.3; counts are a floor, not a complete accounting) (tier inherited from Phase 2)
map.caveat: Uncertain means one direction is indicated but the evidence cannot carry the claim. It is not a weak positive.

map.statement: Sildenafil is the one intervention in this record whose randomised IPF-only evidence points in two directions, with one positive and one null trial and no basis in the record for preferring either.
map.subject: sildenafil
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (conflicting: two credible randomised sources disagree; the record declines to pick)
map.caveat: Conflicting is distinct from Uncertain: two credible bodies of evidence point opposite ways.

map.statement: Every 'works' verdict for a disease-directed drug in this record rests on FVC or a categorical FVC-based composite. Whether a treatment-induced change in FVC decline translates into longer survival is unresolved, and the record forbids grading a lung-function result on the survival dimension.
map.subject: FVC as a surrogate for mortality
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (endpoint-level; carried unresolved from Phase 1)
map.caveat: Preserved as a disagreement; the record does not resolve it.

map.statement: Whether corticosteroids increase mortality in IPF, and by how much, cannot be settled from the available evidence class: the excess-mortality signal comes from pooled predominantly observational data where confounding by indication cannot be excluded, and no randomised monotherapy trial exists.
map.subject: corticosteroid monotherapy
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (evidence-class disagreement; harm verdict retained at a lower tier)
map.caveat: Preserved as a disagreement; the record does not resolve it.

map.statement: Whether a genotype- or telomere-defined subgroup responds differently to N-acetylcysteine is unresolved. The PANTHER monotherapy arm was null overall; the subgroup findings are post hoc and do not lift that verdict.
map.subject: N-acetylcysteine subgroup hypothesis
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Hypothesis (post hoc subgroup; overall randomised result null)
map.caveat: Preserved as a disagreement; the record does not resolve it.

map.statement: Whether co-trimoxazole has any effect in a treatment-adherent subgroup is unresolved: the trial's per-protocol analysis disagreed with its null intention-to-treat result.
map.subject: co-trimoxazole
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (per-protocol vs intention-to-treat disagreement within one trial)
map.caveat: Preserved as a disagreement; the record does not resolve it.

map.section: S4 What we know about the disease
map.statement: IPF is a progressive fibrosing interstitial pneumonia of unknown cause, defined by a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern.
map.subject: disease definition
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Established (current international guideline)
map.caveat: Disease-level facts; they do not license any treatment claim.

map.section: S4 What we know about the disease
map.statement: Pooled global incidence is 5.8 per 100,000 (95% CI 4.8-6.8) and prevalence 17.7 per 100,000 (95% CI 14.0-21.5), with regional variation (North America 27.2, Europe 14.6, Asia 14.8).
map.subject: epidemiology
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Established (systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 incidence and 20 prevalence studies)
map.caveat: Disease-level facts; they do not license any treatment claim.

map.section: S4 What we know about the disease
map.statement: Registry cumulative mortality is 5%, 24%, 37% and 44% at years 1-4, and GAP stage III carries a hazard ratio of 4.64 versus stage I.
map.subject: natural history and prognosis
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Established (prospective national registry)
map.caveat: Disease-level facts; they do not license any treatment claim.

map.section: S4 What we know about the disease
map.statement: Trial populations are not the disease population: 1- and 2-year mortality in modern trial cohorts (6.6%, 13.7%) is far below registry mortality (5%, 24%), which is why mortality endpoints are hard to power and why the randomised evidence base is concentrated in mild-to-moderate physiologic impairment.
map.subject: evidence-base composition
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Established (trial cohort vs registry comparison)
map.caveat: Disease-level facts; they do not license any treatment claim.

map.section: S4 What we know about the disease
map.statement: The frequently quoted median survival of about four years predates antifibrotic therapy (1998 data) and must not be presented as current prognosis.
map.subject: dating of prognostic figures
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Established (era-specific; flagged under scope limit L6)
map.caveat: Disease-level facts; they do not license any treatment claim.

map.section: S4 What we know about the disease
map.statement: Acute exacerbation occurs in 18.6% of patients over three years and carries about 29.5% in-hospital mortality; no intervention in this record prevents or treats it with adequately powered randomised evidence.
map.subject: acute exacerbation
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Established for the epidemiology; the treatment gap is a separate statement (UN6)
map.caveat: Disease-level facts; they do not license any treatment claim.

map.section: S4 What we know about the disease
map.statement: Comorbidity drives outcome: pulmonary hypertension carries a mortality hazard ratio of 2.0 and lung cancer 2.6.
map.subject: comorbidity
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Established (multinational registry)
map.caveat: Disease-level facts; they do not license any treatment claim.

map.section: S4 What we know about the disease
map.statement: The best documented effect on the rate of FVC decline is a 130.1 mL 52-week between-group difference; the least-declining active arm in any IPF trial still declined (-21.5 mL over 26 weeks). No trial has documented recovery of lost lung function.
map.subject: therapeutic ceiling, lung function
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Established (phase 3 and phase 2b randomised trials; ceiling table)
map.caveat: Disease-level facts; they do not license any treatment claim.

map.section: S4 What we know about the disease
map.statement: Antifibrotic therapy is associated with a pooled acute-exacerbation risk ratio of 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, I2=0%), but the pooled sources are predominantly observational.
map.subject: acute exacerbation under treatment
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Uncertain (meta-analysis of predominantly observational data)
map.caveat: Disease-level facts; they do not license any treatment claim.

map.section: S4 What we know about the disease
map.statement: Two interventions are conditionally recommended against for treating IPF by the current guideline: antacid medication and antireflux surgery.
map.subject: guideline-negative interventions
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Established (2022 guideline conditional recommendations against)
map.caveat: Disease-level facts; they do not license any treatment claim.

map.section: S5 What we do not know
map.statement: No intervention has been shown to recover lost lung function in IPF.
map.subject: recovery of lost function
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Unknown (no human trial has demonstrated it; the best result is slower decline)
map.caveat: An absence of evidence is not evidence of promise. Rows M5.7-M5.10 are facts about the record's completeness, not about any intervention.

map.section: S5 What we do not know
map.statement: Reversal of established fibrosis has never been demonstrated in IPF, and no human trial endpoint in this record measures it.
map.subject: reversal
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Unknown (endpoint does not exist in the trial record; not merely unproven)
map.caveat: An absence of evidence is not evidence of promise. Rows M5.7-M5.10 are facts about the record's completeness, not about any intervention.

map.section: S5 What we do not know
map.statement: No drug has randomised evidence of prolonging survival in IPF. The only survival evidence in this record is observational, for lung transplantation.
map.subject: survival
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Unknown (no randomised mortality benefit; mortality endpoints under-powered in trial populations)
map.caveat: An absence of evidence is not evidence of promise. Rows M5.7-M5.10 are facts about the record's completeness, not about any intervention.

map.section: S5 What we do not know
map.statement: Durability of antifibrotic effect beyond 52 weeks has never been established randomly; open-label extensions are not randomised comparisons.
map.subject: durability
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: Unknown (no randomised follow-up beyond 52 weeks)
map.caveat: An absence of evidence is not evidence of promise. Rows M5.7-M5.10 are facts about the record's completeness, not about any intervention.

map.section: S5 What we do not know
map.statement: No validated predictive biomarker identifies which patient benefits from which treatment in IPF; treatment-response heterogeneity is unexplained.

map.statement: Sildenafil does not improve the primary endpoint in the overall IPF population in three randomised trials, including one adding it to pirfenidone in advanced IPF at risk of group 3 pulmonary hypertension. The right-heart-dysfunction subgroup hypothesis derived from exploratory analyses of an earlier trial showed no treatment-by-subgroup heterogeneity when tested in a prespecified analysis.

map.outcome_dimension: E2 disease progression / lung function; E5 symptoms and quality of life
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: three randomised trials plus one prespecified subgroup analysis, consistent null
map.caveat_status: absent in the record - the statement's own qualifications are the only ones recorded

map.statement: Inhaled cromolyn sodium did not reduce chronic cough in IPF in a phase 2b dose-ranging trial, superseding an earlier smaller positive phase 2a trial of the same formulation.
map.subject: cromolyn sodium (RVT-1601)
map.outcome_dimension: E5 symptoms and quality of life
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: one phase 2b randomised trial superseding an earlier positive phase 2a trial
map.caveat_status: absent in the record - the statement's own qualifications are the only ones recorded

map.statement: Bexotegrast is harmful in IPF on the evidence available: an adequately sized randomised phase 2b trial was terminated on DSMB recommendation with more disease-progression events and more deaths on active treatment than on placebo, in both dose arms and in a dose-ordered pattern. In BEACON-IPF (NCT06097260, n=319 randomised), terminated on DSMB recommendation, registry-posted results show more disease-progression events on bexotegrast than placebo: 5 of 106 (placebo), 16 of 105 (160 mg) and 25 of 108 (320 mg); Cox hazard ratios versus placebo 3.31 (95% CI 1.21-9.05, p=0.0194) and 5.36 (95% CI 2.05-13.99, p=0.0006). A >=10% absolute FVC decline was also more frequent (odds ratio 3.33, 95% CI 1.03-10.81, p=0.0449 for 160 mg; 3.01, 95% CI 0.91-9.91, p=0.07 for 320 mg). Deaths: 0 of 106, 6 of 105 and 4 of 108; serious adverse events 6, 17 and 21. The week-52 FVC primary endpoint is uninformative because only 1, 1 and 2 participants reached week 52 after early termination.
map.subject: bexotegrast (PLN-74809)
map.outcome_dimension: E2 disease progression / lung function; E7 survival; E4 safety
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: one adequately sized randomised trial, registry-posted results, terminated early; no peer-reviewed publication of these results identified
map.caveat_status: absent in the record - the statement's own qualifications are the only ones recorded

map.statement: Inhaled GB0139 does not slow lung-function decline in IPF. In GALACTIC-1 (NCT03832946, n=172, quadruple-masked, 52 weeks) the annual rate of FVC decline was -316.60 mL/year (95% CI -394.86 to -238.35) on GB0139 3 mg versus -127.41 mL/year (95% CI -221.12 to -33.71) on placebo, with more respiratory hospitalisations (17 of 102 versus 5 of 70) and worse SGRQ change. No between-arm test is posted and the trial is unpublished, so the apparent harm direction is recorded but not graded as harm.
map.subject: GB0139 (TD139), inhaled galectin-3 inhibitor
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: one adequately sized randomised trial, registry-posted only
map.caveat: Registry posting is the only source; no publication, no statistical comparison, and high attrition in both arms. Conflicts register X12.

map.statement: HZN-825 does not slow lung-function decline in IPF. In NCT05032066 (n=153, triple-masked, 52 weeks) the change in FVC % predicted differed from placebo by -1.13 (95% CI -3.56 to 1.29, p=0.4388) at 300 mg once daily and -0.39 (95% CI -2.86 to 2.09, p=0.7959) at 300 mg twice daily; the sponsor terminated the trial for not meeting primary or key secondary endpoints.
map.subject: HZN-825 (fipaxalparant), oral LPA1 antagonist
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: one adequately sized randomised trial, registry-posted only
map.caveat: Unpublished. Secondary endpoints are internally discordant (worse composite progression on the twice-daily arm, fewer >=10% FVC decliners) - conflicts register X11.

map.statement: Two further neurokinin- and P2X3-directed antitussives do not reduce IPF cough on their trials' primary endpoints. Orvepitant (NCT05185089, n=80 crossover) differed from placebo by 0.00 (95% CI -0.62 to 0.63, p=0.989) at 10 mg and -0.58 (95% CI -1.16 to 0.01, p=0.054) at 30 mg on daily cough severity. Gefapixant (NCT02502097, published PMID 34152585) showed no significant reduction in awake objective cough frequency at day 14 (p=0.90).
map.subject: orvepitant; gefapixant
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: two randomised crossover trials, one published and one registry-posted only
map.caveat: Both trials are short (2-6 weeks) and small; gefapixant's efficacy analysis excluded 7 of 51 randomised patients after a protocol amendment. This adds to the existing negative cough evidence (cromolyn, thalidomide-era work) rather than opening a new question.

map.statement: Whether combined autoantibody reduction (therapeutic plasma exchange plus rituximab plus intravenous immunoglobulin) improves survival after an acute exacerbation of IPF is uncertain and untested by any analysable source. STRIVE-IPF (NCT03286556) posts six-month survival of 44% (SE 9, n=33) versus 7% (SE 6, n=18) on treatment as usual, but the trial is open-label, the arms are unequal from 82 enrolled, no baseline lung function or oxygen requirement is posted, no statistical analysis is posted, and no results publication exists. In stable IPF, blinded rituximab monotherapy was null with numerically more hospitalisations.
map.subject: autoantibody reduction for acute exacerbations of IPF
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: one open-label randomised trial, registry-posted only, plus uncontrolled pilot data
map.caveat: A survival difference of this size in an unblinded trial with unposted baseline severity cannot be separated from case selection. Conflicts register X9. The smallest next step is retrieval of the trial's analysis and publication, not a new trial.
map.phase6_status: added in Phase 6 (C27); held at verification

map.statement: Five investigational programmes now have IPF randomised data that show no signal of benefit but are too small or too truncated to be decisive: LTP001 (n=46, terminated by sponsor decision, FVC % predicted -3.1 versus -1.1), ianalumab (n=30, terminated, FVC difference 0.063 L, p=0.3248), tanzisertib/CC-90001 (n=112 dosed, terminated on a strategic decision, ppFVC differences 1.1 and 2.2 with confidence intervals spanning zero, PMID 38484130), tipelukast (n=15) and belumosudil (open-label, no comparison posted). These are recorded as uncertain, not as failures.
map.subject: small randomised programmes stopped before they could answer their question
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: randomised but underpowered or truncated trials
map.caveat: Sponsor termination for business reasons is not evidence of inefficacy; equally, an unpowered null is not evidence of efficacy. None of these programmes reaches the threshold for a research lead under the Phase 4 screens.

map.statement: A single-centre randomised posting claims a 73.2% reduction in daily coughing episodes versus 16.1% on saline placebo over 21 days in 50 IPF patients (difference -57.13, 95% CI -63.99 to -50.27, p=0.0001), together with a 27.9% rise in the FEV1/FVC ratio and zero adverse events in both arms. There is no publication, no described cough-measurement method and no outcomes-assessor masking, and the accompanying values are not consistent with the known behaviour of IPF over three weeks. The claim is recorded as unverified.
map.subject: sodium pyruvate nasal spray (N115)
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: registry-only, unverifiable against any publication
map.caveat: Recorded because the record must not discard a positive result on the basis of its source; not treated as evidence of benefit because nothing in it can be checked. Conflicts register X10.
map.phase6_status: added in Phase 6 (C29); held at verification

map.section: S5 What we do not know
map.statement: A distinct class of IPF evidence exists that is neither published nor absent: trial results posted to a registry without a between-arm analysis, without a publication, or both. In this record it covers at least nine entities, including two adequately sized phase 2 trials (GALACTIC-1, n=172; HZN-825, n=153) and the only randomised survival result in acute exacerbations (STRIVE-IPF). Registry postings are primary source material and were graded as such, but where the sponsor posts no analysis and publishes no report, the evidence can be described and not weighed.
map.subject: results that exist but cannot be graded
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: fact about the record, not about an intervention
map.caveat: Rows M5.7-M5.13 are facts about the record's completeness, not about any intervention. The remedy is retrieval, not new trials.

map.section: S5 What we do not know
map.statement: The largest single block of randomised IPF evidence that this record has not examined is Chinese-language. English-indexed systematic reviews that searched CNKI, Wanfang, VIP and CBM pool 63 randomised trials of Chinese medicine injections, 23 trials in 1390 patients of qi-supplementing and blood-activating herbs, 20 trials in 1363 patients across four injection products, 11 trials in 981 patients of external TCM treatment, and a herbal-versus-N-acetylcysteine comparison in 733 patients. No injection product and no head-to-head herbal comparison appears in the 279-intervention landscape.
map.subject: Chinese-language randomised evidence not examined by this record
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: fact about the record, not about an intervention
map.caveat: These counts come from secondary sources; the underlying trials were not read and their reviews' own quality statements are cautionary. The counts describe how much evidence exists, not whether any of it shows benefit. No verdict is assigned to any of this evidence.

map.section: S5 What we do not know
map.statement: Non-reporting of completed IPF trials is genuine rather than a search artefact. Of 110 completed trials with no retrievable results, a targeted registry-identifier search of PubMed found any indexed publication for only 7, and none of those reported the trial's missing primary clinical outcome: they were design papers, pre-completion reports, or safety, pharmacokinetic and preclinical papers.
map.subject: unreported completed trials
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: fact about the record, not about an intervention
map.caveat: The search covered PubMed only; results could exist in conference abstracts, theses, regulatory dossiers or non-indexed journals. Two entities were added to the landscape as a result, both phase 1 safety and pharmacokinetics only.

map.statement: The magnitude of corticosteroid harm in IPF is not established, and the direction depends on the setting. The best available synthesis (10 observational studies, 1639 patients with fibrotic ILD) found an uncertain effect on mortality (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.85-1.25) and, in IPF specifically, an uncertain effect on FVC decline (mean difference -3.80% predicted, 95% CI -8.94 to 1.34), both graded very low certainty. In acute exacerbation, one propensity-weighted cohort (n=82, 37 treated) found no association with in-hospital mortality (adjusted HR 1.31) alongside worse overall survival (HR 6.17); a second cohort (n=238) found pulse dosing no better than non-pulse; a third (n=153 and n=229) found early dose tapering associated with better survival (IPW-adjusted HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.14-0.99 and 0.27, 95% CI 0.094-0.83).
map.subject: systemic corticosteroids (monotherapy, excluding the PANTHER triple-therapy regimen)
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: observational evidence only, graded very low certainty by its own authors; confounding by indication is not resolved
map.caveat: None of these studies can separate a corticosteroid effect from the severity that prompted the prescription. The record's separate finding of harm from prednisone plus azathioprine plus N-acetylcysteine (PANTHER-IPF) is randomised evidence about a three-drug regimen and does not transfer to corticosteroid monotherapy. The tapering result is about how long steroids are continued, not whether they help.

map.section: S5 What we do not know
map.statement: FVC is a validated prognostic marker in IPF but has not been validated as a treatment-effect surrogate. Patient-level evidence is strong: in pooled nintedanib trial data (n=2583) a faster rate of FVC decline and a lower current FVC each predicted death over 52 weeks (HR 1.79, 95% CI 1.57-2.03 and HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.17-1.32 per 5-percentage-point decrease), and in a prospective registry, adjusted declines of at least 2%, 5% and 10% predicted were associated with 1.8-, 2.3- and 2.7-fold increases in the risk of death or transplantation. What no published analysis establishes is the trial-level question: whether a drug's effect on FVC predicts its effect on survival.
map.subject: FVC as a surrogate endpoint
map.outcome_dimension: surrogacy of the record's primary outcome measure
map.evidence_tier_sublabel: fact about the record's outcome measure, not about an intervention
map.caveat: Patient-level prognostic association is not surrogacy. Every 'slows progression' verdict in this record rests on FVC, so this gap propagates to those verdicts: it does not make them wrong, but it means the survival consequence of the observed FVC benefit is inferred rather than measured. Individual IPF trials are underpowered for mortality, so the trial-level analysis is unlikely to be informative without pooled individual participant data.

conflicts.subject: co-trimoxazole
conflicts.description: Shulgina 2013 (PMID 23143842) reported no FVC effect but a per-protocol all-cause mortality reduction; EME-TIPAC (PMID 33165623 family) was null on its primary. Logged in the conflicts register.
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: A larger adequately powered trial reporting the same comparison supersedes the smaller one; the residual adherence question is recorded as an open question, not as a conflict.

conflicts.subject: n-acetylcysteine
conflicts.description: Post hoc pharmacogenomic and telomere-length subgroup analyses of the same trial data report differential effects (PMID 30566847 and the TOLLIP hypothesis behind NCT04300920); logged as an unresolved subgroup question (UN11), not as a positive result.

conflicts.subject: pamrevlumab
conflicts.description: PRAISE phase 2 positive (PMID 31575509) vs ZEPHYRUS-1 phase 3 null (PMID 38762797); logged in the conflicts register as resolved-by-supersession.
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: brief section 2 evidence hierarchy: a larger randomised trial on the same endpoint supersedes a smaller one

conflicts.subject: sildenafil
conflicts.description: 1 positive vs 1 null randomised IPF-only sources
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: Three randomised trials are null in the overall IPF population, and the right-heart-dysfunction subgroup hypothesis showed no treatment-by-subgroup heterogeneity when tested prospectively in a prespecified analysis; the remaining disagreement is between overall nulls and exploratory subgroup analyses, which does not meet the definition of a within-intervention conflict.
conflicts.verdict_recorded: Failed in the overall population; subgroup hypothesis tested and not supported

conflicts.subject: FVC as a surrogate for mortality
conflicts.description: Every 'Works' verdict in this landscape rests on FVC or a categorical FVC-based composite. Phase 1 found no retrieved source establishing trial-level surrogacy of FVC change for mortality; nor was surrogacy refuted. Antifibrotic survival evidence is pooled observational (RR 0.55) rather than randomised.
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: brief section 2 prohibits grading a lung-function result on the survival dimension; no drug is graded as improving survival
conflicts.verdict_recorded: applies to pirfenidone, nintedanib, nerandomilast, inhaled treprostinil

conflicts.subject: corticosteroid monotherapy
conflicts.description: Pooled largely observational data report excess mortality with corticosteroids, and the randomised harm evidence belongs to the prednisone+azathioprine+NAC combination, not to steroid monotherapy, which has never been randomised in IPF. Steroids nonetheless remain in use for acute exacerbation, where no treatment has randomised support.
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: tier capped at Uncertain because the pooled sources are predominantly observational

conflicts.subject: N-acetylcysteine subgroup hypothesis
conflicts.conflict_type: post hoc subgroup vs overall null
conflicts.description: The PANTHER NAC arm was null overall (PMID 24836309), while post hoc telomere-length and TOLLIP genotype analyses of the same trial data report differential effects. A prospective genotype-stratified trial (NCT04300920) was launched on that basis.
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: post hoc subgroup findings do not lift the overall verdict; recorded as an open question (UN11) | PHASE4 CORRECTION (C19): the register cited PMID 30566847 (telomere length and immunosuppression) as the source of the N-acetylcysteine subgroup hypothesis. The primary source is PMID 26331942 (TOLLIP rs3750920 x N-acetylcysteine interaction in PANTHER-IPF). Both are retained as distinct subgroup hypotheses.

conflicts.subject: traditional Chinese medicine formulas
conflicts.description: Three randomised IPF-only TCM trials reach screen tier T1 and nine more reach T2, with author-reported benefit in most. None was independently replicated outside its originating setting, risk of bias could only be judged from abstracts, and CNKI/VIP/Wanfang/SinoMed were not searched, so both the count and the direction may be biased in unknown magnitude.
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: brief section 4.3 caps every such row at Uncertain

conflicts.subject: autoantibody reduction (plasma exchange + rituximab + IVIG)
conflicts.conflict_type: setting-dependent disagreement, unblinded positive versus blinded null
conflicts.description: STRIVE-IPF (NCT03286556), open-label randomised, posts six-month survival of 44% (SE 9, n=33) on autoantibody reductive therapy versus 7% (SE 6, n=18) on treatment as usual in acute exacerbations of IPF, with no statistical analysis and no results publication. In stable IPF, a triple-masked randomised trial of rituximab monotherapy (NCT01969409, n=58) met only its autoantibody-titre primary endpoint and showed no benefit on FVC, survival or transplant-free survival, with 12 versus 6 hospital admissions and 9 of 30 versus 5 of 28 serious adverse events.
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: none; the two results address different clinical settings (acute exacerbation versus stable disease) and different regimens (triple therapy versus rituximab alone), so neither supersedes the other. Both are recorded; the survival signal is not treated as evidence of benefit while its analysis and publication are missing.

conflicts.subject: sodium pyruvate nasal spray (N115)
conflicts.conflict_type: registry-only positive result with internal implausibility
conflicts.description: NCT06037408 (n=50, single site, sponsor Cellular Sciences) posts a 73.2% reduction in daily coughing episodes versus 16.1% on saline (difference -57.13, 95% CI -63.99 to -50.27, p=0.0001) after 21 days, alongside a 27.9% increase in the FEV1/FVC ratio versus 2.73% (p<0.0001) and zero adverse events in both arms. No publication exists, the cough measurement method is not described, and no outcomes-assessor masking is stated.
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: none; the effect sizes and the zero-adverse-event count are not consistent with the known behaviour of IPF over three weeks, and no source beyond the registry posting exists to check them against. Recorded as an unverified claim, not as evidence of benefit.

conflicts.subject: HZN-825 (fipaxalparant) secondary endpoints
conflicts.description: In NCT05032066 the 300 mg twice-daily arm shows a worse composite progression-free survival than placebo (hazard ratio 2.52, 95% CI 1.22 to 5.61, p=0.0438) while simultaneously showing fewer participants with a >=10% FVC decline (odds ratio 0.469, 95% CI 0.236 to 0.934, p=0.0706). The primary FVC endpoint is null in both dose arms.
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: the prespecified primary endpoint governs the verdict; the discordant secondaries are recorded rather than interpreted, and neither is treated as a harm finding or a benefit finding on its own.

conflicts.subject: GB0139 (TD139) GALACTIC-1
conflicts.description: The primary endpoint of GALACTIC-1 (NCT03832946, n=172) is posted as arm-level annual FVC decline with non-overlapping confidence intervals - GB0139 3 mg -316.60 mL/year (95% CI -394.86 to -238.35) versus placebo -127.41 mL/year (95% CI -221.12 to -33.71) - together with more respiratory hospitalisations (17 of 102 versus 5 of 70) and worse SGRQ change, but no between-arm statistical test is posted and the trial is unpublished. Attrition was high in both arms (completion 55 of 102 and 38 of 70).
conflicts.resolution_rule_applied: graded Failed on the direction of the prespecified primary endpoint, which is unfavourable; the apparent harm direction is not upgraded to a harm verdict because no formal comparison, adjustment for attrition, or peer-reviewed report is available. No statistical test was computed here from the posted summaries.

leads_outcome.statement: Phase 4 promoted no research lead. Forty-one candidate signals were screened against six prespecified screens; none met the promotion bar. Four are held at verification because their key result could not be checked against primary full text, and are neither promoted nor rejected. Phase 5 (deep investigation of surviving leads) was therefore recorded as skipped because there was nothing to investigate, not as not done.
leads_outcome.not_a_therapeutic_claim: A held candidate is a verification state, not a positive finding, and an unretrieved or missing result is not evidence of promise.

candidates.subject: azithromycin
candidates.reason: The abandonment and the null belong to different trials (C22). The chronic-cough question has a randomised crossover answer (NCT02173145, PMID 34015241) and the terminated trial was a combination-therapy study (NCT01432080, n=12). The ongoing 1000-patient trial NCT05842681 addresses acute exacerbation management, a different question, and is recorded as such rather than as an answer to this candidate.

candidates.subject: losartan
candidates.reason: Human IPF evidence is one open-label single-arm study (n=20) and one randomised trial terminated at n=12 with registry-posted results. Neither can establish a signal in a disease with highly variable individual FVC trajectories, and no ongoing IPF programme targets the angiotensin pathway.

candidates.subject: cromolyn sodium (RVT-1601)
candidates.reason: Not abandoned before a result: a phase 2b dose-ranging trial was null on cough (C15), superseding the earlier positive phase 2a.

candidates.subject: continuous positive airway pressure
candidates.reason: IPF evidence is two small studies (n=12 completed, n=7 terminated) with no randomised comparison against an IPF outcome. Where obstructive sleep apnoea coexists, CPAP is indicated on its own grounds; that is comorbidity management, not an IPF-progression hypothesis.

candidates.subject: GLPG1205
candidates.shape: (a) unreplicated null that size or phase cannot make decisive
candidates.reason: A phase 2 trial (n=68, results posted) was null on FVC. An underpowered null contains no positive signal, and the record holds no prior - mechanistic, subgroup or otherwise - that would justify retesting GPR84 antagonism at size. No ongoing programme.

candidates.reason: One phase 2 trial (n=88, 2003-2007), null. No signal to retest and no ongoing programme; TNF blockade in IPF has not been revisited in over 15 years.

candidates.subject: imatinib

candidates.reason: One phase 2/3 trial (n=120), null on time to disease progression. No ongoing IPF programme.

candidates.shape: (a) unreplicated null that size or phase cannot make decisive

candidates.subject: macitentan
candidates.shape: (a) unreplicated null that size or phase cannot make decisive
candidates.reason: One phase 2 trial (n=178), null on FVC. The class question is not open: bosentan was null in two trials and ambrisentan was harmful in ARTEMIS-IPF, so endothelin-receptor antagonism has a class-level answer in IPF.

candidates.subject: n-acetylcysteine in a TOLLIP- or telomere-defined subgroup
candidates.reason: The motivating result is a post hoc TOLLIP rs3750920 x N-acetylcysteine interaction in PANTHER-IPF (PMID 26331942; provenance corrected in C19). Its full text is closed access and could not be obtained, so under the Phase 4 brief it is verification-incomplete. Separately, the genotype-stratified phase 3 trial PRECISIONS (NCT04300920) has completed with no results posted, so the question is already being answered and the smallest next step is retrieval, not a new hypothesis. Carried to Phase 6 as a retrieval action.

candidates.subject: co-trimoxazole adherence-dependent effect
candidates.outcome: rejected as a lead; analysis action retained
candidates.reason: The intention-to-treat null now rests on EME-TIPAC (n=342, C13), which supersedes the smaller trial. Whether adherence modifies the effect is a re-analysis of existing trial data, not an intervention hypothesis; carried to Phase 6 as an analysis action with the caveat that per-protocol comparisons in an open-label context are confounded by health status.

candidates.subject: sildenafil in right-heart dysfunction
candidates.reason: The subgroup hypothesis has been tested (C14): a prespecified INSTAGE subgroup analysis found no treatment-by-subgroup heterogeneity on SGRQ or FVC, and a phase 2b trial prospectively enrolled the enriched at-risk-of-pulmonary-hypertension population and was null on its primary endpoint. The trialists' residual call for further subgroup research is preserved in the map as an open statement, but no positive subgroup result supports it.

candidates.subject: BMS-986020 / LPA1 pathway
candidates.reason: The pathway question is under test: admilparant (BMS-986278) has a positive phase 2 (n=403) and an active phase 3 (NCT06003426, n=1255) with a second phase 3 planned (NCT07441408). Reviving the abandoned molecule adds nothing that the successor trial will not answer; its own stopping reason was drug-related hepatobiliary toxicity (C18).

candidates.subject: FVC change as a surrogate for survival
candidates.outcome: rejected as a lead; analysis action retained
candidates.reason: A surrogacy question about an endpoint, not a therapeutic hypothesis. It is answerable by trial-level or individual-participant meta-analysis of existing trials. Whether published meta-analyses already answer it was not assessed in Phase 4; a prior literature check is part of the Phase 6 action.

candidates.subject: 110 completed trials with unretrievable results
candidates.outcome: rejected as a lead; retrieval action retained
candidates.reason: Missing results are a gap in the record, not evidence of therapeutic promise - the Phase 4 brief forbids converting one into the other. Retrieval remains the largest single addition available to this record and is carried to Phase 6.

candidates.subject: Jinbei oral liquid
candidates.reason: Full text verified (C20): no primary endpoint was predefined, the single significant endpoint (total lung capacity) sits among many tested with no multiplicity control, and no accepted IPF efficacy endpoint was met.

candidates.subject: Kangxian Huanji granule
candidates.reason: The abstract reports treatment failure at 4 weeks with RR 0.22 (95% CI 0.051-0.965, P=0.023) and a non-significant 16-week mortality difference, but the full text could not be obtained through any available route. Under the Phase 4 brief this is verification-incomplete and cannot be promoted. Obtaining the full text is carried to Phase 6.

candidates.subject: Baduanjin exercise
candidates.reason: Full text verified (C21): n=28, 8 weeks, unblinded, allocation by opened envelopes, authors describe it as exploratory, and the control group received no training at all. Against a no-exercise comparator the result cannot be separated from the generic effect of exercise training, which the record already grades at Probable.

candidates.subject: Chinese-language database gap
candidates.outcome: rejected as a lead; retrieval action retained
candidates.reason: A search-coverage limitation (CNKI, VIP, Wanfang, SinoMed were not searchable from this environment), not a therapeutic hypothesis. Carried to Phase 6.

candidates.subject: corticosteroid harm magnitude
candidates.outcome: rejected as a lead; analysis action retained
candidates.reason: A harm-quantification question answerable in existing cohorts, with confounding by indication as the central methodological problem. Not an intervention hypothesis.

candidates.subject: recovery and reversal endpoints
candidates.outcome: rejected as a lead; measurement action retained
candidates.reason: No intervention in the record targets recovery of lost lung function and no trial endpoint measures it. This is an endpoint-development question; naming it as a therapeutic lead would invert the brief's rule that a gap is not a hypothesis.

candidates.subject: pulmonary rehabilitation durability
candidates.shape: (g) open question about an intervention that works
candidates.reason: Answered to 52 weeks by a randomised trial the Phase 2 search missed (C12), which is null on 6MWD and favours training on endurance time. The residual untested horizon is beyond 12 months; it remains an open statement in the map, not a lead.

candidates.subject: omeprazole
candidates.reason: Full-text verification weakened rather than supported the signal (C17): feasibility was the primary objective, no formal sample-size calculation was performed, the adjusted cough-frequency interval includes no effect, and FEV1 and FVC differences in the same trial favour placebo, with more lower respiratory tract infections on omeprazole.

candidates.subject: GSK3008348
candidates.reason: Phase 1 only, with a phase 1b terminated at n=8 (results posted). The primary endpoints were safety and target engagement (C16); there is no clinical-outcome signal to follow up.

candidates.subject: LTI-03
candidates.reason: Phase 1 primary endpoints were safety and tolerability (C16), and a phase 2 trial (NCT06968845, n=120) is recruiting. The question is already being answered by an appropriately designed trial.

candidates.subject: TRK-250
candidates.reason: One phase 1 trial (n=34, results posted 2023) with a safety primary endpoint and no clinical outcome; no subsequent programme.

candidates.subject: bexotegrast (PLN-74809)
candidates.reason: Superseded by its own trial (C23): the phase 2b BEACON-IPF was terminated on DSMB recommendation with excess disease-progression events and deaths on active treatment. The intervention moves to the harm register, not to a lead.

candidates.subject: omipalisib
candidates.reason: A single mechanistic study with an FDG-PET uptake primary endpoint (C16); no clinical outcome and no subsequent programme.

candidates.subject: salbutamol
candidates.reason: Randomised data address lung deposition and short-term physiology, not a clinical outcome (C16).

candidates.subject: sirolimus
candidates.reason: The trial's primary endpoint was not a clinical outcome and its own abstract states 'Lung function was unaffected by either treatment' (C16).

candidates.subject: valganciclovir
candidates.reason: Randomised human data address a virological or safety endpoint, not a clinical IPF outcome (C16). The only recently posted valganciclovir result in the registry extract is a CMV-prophylaxis trial after lung transplantation, which is outside this record's scope.

candidates.subject: palliative care
candidates.reason: The randomised evidence addresses feasibility and process endpoints (C16). Palliative and supportive care is already recommended in IPF guidelines and graded in the map; the open question is implementation, not whether an effect exists to discover.

candidates.subject: mesenchymal stem cells
candidates.reason: All completed IPF trials are phase 1 or 1/2 with safety primary endpoints and 8-24 participants (C16), and several early-phase trials are ongoing, including a phase 2 (NCT07131150, n=66). No clinical signal exists yet to promote.

candidates.subject: autoantibody reduction (plasma exchange + rituximab + IVIG) for acute exacerbations of IPF
candidates.reason: The signal is the largest single positive randomised result in the whole record: six-month survival 44% (SE 9, n=33) versus 7% (SE 6, n=18) in STRIVE-IPF (NCT03286556). It fails S5 because the only source is a registry posting with no statistical analysis, no baseline lung function or oxygen requirement, unequal arms drawn from 82 enrolled, no masking of any party, and no results publication - only a design paper (PMID 38509495). It also fails S3: NCT07299695 (phase 3 intravenous immunoglobulin in acute exacerbations, recruiting) and NCT07674745 (autoantibody reduction in progressive IPF, not yet recruiting) are registered and address the same question. Smallest next step is retrieval of the STRIVE-IPF analysis and publication (action A10), not a new trial.

candidates.subject: sodium pyruvate nasal spray (N115) for IPF cough
candidates.reason: NCT06037408 posts a -57.13 percentage-point between-arm difference in daily coughing episodes (p=0.0001) at a single site in 50 patients. It fails S5: there is no publication, the cough-measurement method is not described, outcomes-assessor masking is not stated, and the accompanying values (a 27.9% rise in the FEV1/FVC ratio over 21 days, zero adverse events in 50 IPF patients in both arms) cannot be reconciled with the known behaviour of the disease. Nothing in the posting can be checked against a primary report. Smallest next step is retrieval of a protocol, analysis plan and publication (action A11).

candidates.subject: tanzisertib (CC-90001), oral JNK inhibitor
candidates.reason: NCT03142191 (n=112 dosed) was stopped for a sponsor strategic decision, not for a result, and the published ppFVC differences favour active drug numerically: 1.1% (95% CI -2.1 to 4.3, p=0.50) at 200 mg and 2.2% (95% CI -1.1 to 5.4, p=0.19) at 400 mg (PMID 38484130). By the same rule applied to GLPG1205 at P5, a non-significant null contains no positive signal to retest; there is no ongoing IPF programme for the molecule. Recorded as Uncertain in the landscape rather than promoted.

candidates.subject: LTP001
candidates.shape: (a) unreplicated null that size or phase cannot make decisive
candidates.reason: NCT05497284 (n=46, terminated by sponsor decision) is numerically worse on the primary FVC endpoint (-3.1 versus -1.1 % predicted; Bayesian slope -2.6, 95% credible interval -6.9 to 1.3). An underpowered null with an unfavourable direction contains no positive signal (rule as applied at P5).

candidates.subject: ianalumab (VAY736)
candidates.shape: (a) unreplicated null that size or phase cannot make decisive
candidates.reason: NCT03287414 (n=30, terminated by sponsor decision) shows an FVC difference of 0.063 L (95% CI -0.115 to 0.241, p=0.3248). No positive signal; no ongoing IPF programme.

candidates.subject: tipelukast (MN-001)
candidates.shape: (a) unreplicated null that size or phase cannot make decisive
candidates.reason: NCT02503657 (n=15) posts FVC change -0.177 L on MN-001 versus -0.025 L in the comparator arm with no between-arm analysis. Too small to contain an interpretable signal in either direction.

candidates.subject: belumosudil (KD025)
candidates.reason: NCT02688647 posts stable FVC on belumosudil (2608.2 to 2626.8 mL) against a decline on best supportive care (2516.7 to 2438.1 mL) at 24 weeks, but the trial is open-label with no blinding and no posted between-arm comparison, so the difference is not separable from the absence of a control condition. No clinical signal that survives the screen.

candidates.subject: rituximab monotherapy in stable IPF
candidates.shape: (a) unreplicated null that size or phase cannot make decisive
candidates.reason: NCT01969409 (n=58, triple-masked) met a mechanistic autoantibody-titre primary endpoint and showed no benefit on FVC, survival or transplant-free survival, with 12 versus 6 hospital admissions and 9 of 30 versus 5 of 28 serious adverse events. No positive clinical signal; the combination-therapy question in acute exacerbations is carried separately at P34.

screens.definition: retrieval artefact - the question already had an answer the earlier record missed
superseded - a later or larger result, or the programme's own posted result, replaces the signal
already being answered - a registered ongoing trial addresses the same question
no testable signal - no controlled human signal, a non-clinical primary endpoint, or an effect not separable from an already-graded intervention
verification incomplete - the key result could not be checked against primary full text
not a therapeutic lead - a record, analysis or measurement action rather than an intervention hypothesis

corrections.claim_corrected: Phase 0 open question Q3 described PRECISIONS (NCT04300920) as 'unretrievable'.
corrections.correction: The registry snapshot taken 2026-09-02 gives a completion date of 2026-03-02, so the trial is within the 12-month reporting window. It is reclassified from 'unretrievable' to 'no results found (within reporting window)'. Phase 0's underlying statements (completed, no results posted, only a design paper indexed) remain accurate.
corrections.basis: ClinicalTrials.gov API completion date field, retrieved 2026-09-02
corrections.effect: UN11 and the retrievability register use the corrected classification. Q3 remains open.

corrections.correction: That count used trial START date. Counting by registry-recorded COMPLETION date gives 134 completed 2010 or later without posted results, of which 102 have no post-completion publication either. The Phase 1 register reports completion-date-based counts throughout.

corrections.effect: Phase 1 headline counts (239 / 90 / 39 / 110 / 97) supersede the Phase 0 counts for retrievability claims.

corrections.basis: Scope audit against the Phase 0 report, 2026-09-02

corrections.claim_corrected: IPF_SCOPE.md Part C left six criteria unfixed (TCM thresholds, whether risk of bias gates inclusion, non-English database coverage, curated-intervention inclusion threshold, the survival-grading bar, cross-trial FVC admissibility).
corrections.correction: All six are now prespecified in IPF_PHASE2_BRIEF.md, written before any Phase 2 treatment effect was retrieved. Numeric TCM thresholds were replaced by design-based tiers T1-T5 rather than being set: the corpus distribution is reported instead of converted into a cutoff, and studies failing the T1 bar move down a tier and keep their row. Risk of bias is reported and caps the verdict rather than gating inclusion. Cross-trial quantitative FVC comparison is declared inadmissible.
corrections.basis: IPF_SCOPE.md Part C; Phase 1 endpoint taxonomy findings on placebo drift and absent surrogacy validation
corrections.effect: Phase 2 grading and the TCM screen follow the brief; the brief is published with the record.

corrections.claim_corrected: Evidence-to-intervention attribution rebuilt three times
corrections.correction: Evidence was first attached to an intervention by which entity's PubMed query returned the abstract. That let a harm signal from a shared multi-arm abstract propagate to every agent named in it. Attribution is now taken from each extraction's own intervention list, with comparator-only mentions excluded.
corrections.basis: Phase 2 grading run, 2026-09-02; inspection of the resulting strong-verdict rows against the retrieved abstracts

corrections.claim_corrected: Role classifier added (monotherapy / combination or head-to-head / pooled many-agent)
corrections.correction: Network meta-analyses listing many agents were spreading a single direction across all of them. Pooled many-agent sources are now kept as context but excluded from direction counting. A first version of this rule misread multi-dose arms of one agent as multiple interventions, which briefly left two phase 3 programmes with no monotherapy evidence; fixed by treating listed interventions that all contain the entity's own name variants as monotherapy.
corrections.basis: Phase 2 grading run, 2026-09-02; inspection of the resulting strong-verdict rows against the retrieved abstracts
corrections.effect: ipf_phase2_landscape.csv columns n_mono_randomised, pooled_context_pmids

corrections.claim_corrected: Model-based grading abandoned in favour of an explicit rule engine plus documented manual curation
corrections.correction: The per-session model budget was exhausted. The rule engine is also auditable: every verdict is reproducible from the recorded columns, and 25 rows carry an explicit curation_note stating what was overridden and why.
corrections.basis: Phase 2 grading run, 2026-09-02; inspection of the resulting strong-verdict rows against the retrieved abstracts
corrections.effect: ipf_phase2_landscape.csv column curated / curation_note

corrections.claim_corrected: Traditional-medicine record classifier rewritten around PubMed publication types; four tiers corrected by hand
corrections.correction: A first pass keyed on abstract wording classified a block of narrative reviews and mechanistic papers as non-randomised human evidence. The rewritten rule requires publication-type evidence plus explicit human enrolment. Four borderline records were then corrected with stated reasons (PMIDs 30616998, 41184899, 33164264, 36857968).
corrections.basis: Phase 2 grading run, 2026-09-02; inspection of the resulting strong-verdict rows against the retrieved abstracts
corrections.effect: ipf_phase2_traditional_medicine_screen.csv columns tier, tier_reason, tier_manually_corrected

corrections.claim_corrected: Lung transplantation added as a curated landscape row
corrections.correction: Transplantation is a procedure, not a trial arm label, so it was absent from both the registry intervention universe and the per-entity literature search. Its survival figure is read back from the Phase 1 ceiling table and is registry-based, so it is capped under the brief's survival rule.
corrections.basis: Phase 2 grading run, 2026-09-02; inspection of the resulting strong-verdict rows against the retrieved abstracts
corrections.effect: ipf_phase2_landscape.csv row 'lung transplantation'; ipf_phase1_ceiling.csv

corrections.claim_corrected: Phase 2 report and 9 landscape rows cited E-codes that do not match ipf_phase1_endpoint_taxonomy.csv: categorical progression as E7, functional capacity as E13, HRQoL/SGRQ as E11, survival as E15, cough as E10, acute exacerbation as E9.
corrections.correction: Corrected to the taxonomy: categorical progression E3, functional capacity E5, HRQoL SGRQ E6, survival E11, cough E9, acute exacerbation E10. Dimension names and all results were already correct; only the codes were wrong, so no verdict, tier or effect estimate changed.
corrections.basis: Row-by-row audit of every E-code string in ipf_phase2_landscape.csv and IPF_phase2_treatment_landscape.md against the Phase 1 taxonomy, 2026-09-02, at the start of Phase 3.
corrections.effect: Phase 3 map and Phase 4 lead screening use the corrected codes. Both Phase 2 files re-issued as new versions.

corrections.claim_corrected: Phase 2 graded 17 entities with a PHASE3 registry label as 'Poorly studied - no IPF-specific human outcome evidence retrieved'. For six of them the primary report exists and was missed by the per-entity search: ziritaxestat (ISABELA 1/2), deupirfenidone (ELEVATE-IPF, already cited in the Phase 1 ceiling table), admilparant, INS018_055/rentosertib, ART-123/thrombomodulin alfa and NAL ER/nalbuphine ER. ziritaxestat was also filed in the negative register as 'development stopped before a result was established', and 'co-trimoxazole or doxycycline' was carried as an ungraded duplicate of the CleanUP-IPF evidence. The Phase 1 cough ceiling cited low-dose morphine as the best documented result.
corrections.correction: Retrieval-artefact check run before Phase 4 on all 17 phase-3-labelled 'Poorly studied' entities. Six reclassified from the retrieved abstracts: ziritaxestat -> Failed (Established; null primary endpoint in both phase 3 trials), ART-123 -> Failed (Probable; day-90 survival 72.5% vs 89.2% placebo), deupirfenidone -> Uncertain (Probable; one phase 2b positive at 26 weeks), admilparant -> Uncertain (IPF-cohort CI includes zero; the significant estimate is the separate PPF cohort), INS018_055 -> Uncertain (Hypothesis; safety primary endpoint, exploratory FVC signal), NAL ER -> Works on cough (E9) only (Probable; two randomised trials, <=6 weeks, both sponsor-run). ziritaxestat moved in the negative register from 'development stopped' to 'no benefit on the trial's own primary endpoint'; ART-123 and the CleanUP-IPF strategy label added there. The Phase 1 cough ceiling row now cites CORAL (60.2% relative reduction vs 16.9% placebo at 6 weeks) and CANAL alongside PACIFY COUGH. The other eleven entities (AK3280, EZ-2053, HEC585, HSK44459, TDI01, minocycline, azathioprine monotherapy, lansoprazole, sodium pyruvate, methylprednisolone/prednisone monotherapy, and the doxycycline label) returned no IPF randomised report and stay 'Poorly studied'.
corrections.basis: Targeted PubMed retrieval on 2026-09-02 with drug-name and trial-acronym synonyms plus publication-type filtering, run on the 17 entities. Every reclassified row carries a verbatim quote checked as an exact substring of its own abstract. Searches recorded in ipf_phase3_retrieval_check.json.
corrections.effect: Landscape verdicts change from 6 Works / 8 Failed / 8 Harm outweighs benefit / 1 Conflicting / 43 Uncertain / 215 Poorly studied to 7 Works / 11 Failed / 8 Harm outweighs benefit / 1 Conflicting / 46 Uncertain / 208 Poorly studied (the eleventh Failed row is the resolved CleanUP-IPF duplicate label). Phase 4 must not treat any of these six as an evidence gap. Establishes that the Phase 2 per-entity search under-retrieves for agents whose registry label is a code name or a two-drug string; the residual 208 'Poorly studied' rows are therefore an upper bound on genuine absence of evidence.

corrections.claim_corrected: Phase 2 and map statement M6.9 held that no randomised trial had tested whether pulmonary rehabilitation gains persist beyond 3-6 months, and rated durability an open question.
corrections.correction: A 52-week randomised trial of exercise training on background antifibrotic therapy (PMID 37012071) exists and was missed. It is null on 6MWD ('mean difference, 21 m (95% CI -25 to 66), p=0.38') and favours training on endurance time ('mean difference, 187 s (95% CI 34 to 153), p=0.019'). The untested horizon is now beyond 12 months, not beyond 6 months.
corrections.basis: Phase 4 screen-1 search (rehabilitation synonyms) 2026-09-03; abstract read. The endurance-time interval as printed does not contain its own point estimate; reproduced verbatim and flagged as an apparent source typographical error - full text not obtained.
corrections.effect: Landscape curation note and M1.6 amended; candidate P22 (durability) rejected as already answered.

corrections.claim_corrected: Phase 2 held a smaller co-trimoxazole trial as the key result and carried an unresolved intention-to-treat versus per-protocol conflict (X1).
corrections.correction: The adequately powered EME-TIPAC trial (n=342, PMID 33289822) was missed. Its primary time-to-event composite is null ('hazard ratio of 1.2 ([95% CI, 0.9-1.6]; P = .32)'). X1 is resolved by supersession; the adherence question survives only as a re-analysis action.
corrections.basis: Phase 4 screen-1 search (co-trimoxazole/trimethoprim synonyms) 2026-09-03; abstract read.
corrections.effect: Landscape key result, negative-results register and M2.3 updated; X1 status changed; candidate P11 rejected as superseded, re-analysis carried to Phase 6.

corrections.claim_corrected: Phase 2 and Phase 3 recorded sildenafil as the record's only genuinely conflicting intervention (X4) and listed a right-heart-dysfunction subgroup as an open question (M6.5).
corrections.correction: Two randomised sources were missed: a phase 2b trial adding sildenafil to pirfenidone in advanced IPF at risk of group 3 pulmonary hypertension, null on its primary endpoint ('between-group difference 3·06% [95% CI -11·30 to 17·97]; p=0·65'), and a prespecified INSTAGE subgroup analysis ('There was no heterogeneity between subgroups by presence of RHD in the effect of nintedanib plus sildenafil versus nintedanib alone on change in SGRQ total score at Week 12 (P = 0.74) or Week 24 (P = 0.90), or change in FVC at Week 12 (P = 0.58) or Week 24 (P = 0.55)'). Sildenafil is reclassified Failed in the overall population and the subgroup hypothesis is recorded as tested and not supported. The trialists' own residual sentence ('further research is required to establish if specific subgroups of patients with IPF might benefit from sildenafil') is preserved as an open statement not backed by a positive subgroup result.
corrections.basis: Phase 4 screen-1 search (sildenafil synonyms) 2026-09-03; both abstracts read.
corrections.effect: Landscape verdict changed Conflicting->Failed; X4 resolved; new map statement M2.13; M3.10 and M6.5 superseded; candidate P12 rejected.

corrections.claim_corrected: Phase 2 graded cromolyn sodium (RVT-1601) as a programme stopped before a result and listed it as abandoned rather than refuted (M6.1, M3.5).
corrections.correction: A phase 2a trial of the same inhaled formulation was positive on cough (PMID 28923239) and a larger phase 2b dose-ranging trial was null ('did not provide benefit over placebo for the treatment of chronic cough in patients with IPF'). The programme was superseded by its own null result, not abandoned before one.
corrections.basis: Phase 4 screen-2 search (cromolyn/RVT-1601 synonyms) 2026-09-03; abstracts read.
corrections.effect: Landscape verdict changed to Failed; negative-results register row reclassified; new map statement M2.14; removed from M3.5 and M6.1; candidate P3 rejected as superseded.

Sub-labels rewritten; M6.11 rewritten to state that only BMS-986020 has a positive clinical-endpoint result among these.

corrections.claim_corrected: Phase 2 recorded azithromycin's abandonment reason as recruitment_or_operational alongside a null cough result, and M6.1 listed it as abandoned rather than refuted.
corrections.correction: The two facts belong to different trials: the null cough result is a completed double-blind randomised crossover trial (NCT02173145, PMID 34015241, 'This randomized controlled trial does not support the use of low-dose azithromycin for chronic cough in patients with IPF'), while the terminated trial was a combination-therapy study (NCT01432080, n=12). The cough question has a randomised answer.
corrections.basis: Registry rows for NCT02173145, NCT01432080 and NCT05842681 read from the Phase 0 registry extract, Phase 4 2026-09-03.
corrections.effect: Landscape curation note and M6.1 amended; candidate P1 rejected - the abandoned trial is not the source of the signal, and the ongoing large trial NCT05842681 addresses acute exacerbation, a different question.

corrections.claim_corrected: Phase 2 graded bexotegrast as a positive randomised signal below phase 3 (later corrected in C16 to a non-clinical primary endpoint) and Phase 3 listed it among small programmes awaiting adequately sized follow-up (M6.11).
corrections.correction: Bexotegrast is reclassified as 'Harm outweighs benefit'. In BEACON-IPF (NCT06097260, n=319 randomised), terminated on DSMB recommendation, registry-posted results show more disease-progression events on bexotegrast than placebo: 5 of 106 (placebo), 16 of 105 (160 mg) and 25 of 108 (320 mg); Cox hazard ratios versus placebo 3.31 (95% CI 1.21-9.05, p=0.0194) and 5.36 (95% CI 2.05-13.99, p=0.0006). A >=10% absolute FVC decline was also more frequent (odds ratio 3.33, 95% CI 1.03-10.81, p=0.0449 for 160 mg; 3.01, 95% CI 0.91-9.91, p=0.07 for 320 mg). Deaths: 0 of 106, 6 of 105 and 4 of 108; serious adverse events 6, 17 and 21. The week-52 FVC primary endpoint is uninformative because only 1, 1 and 2 participants reached week 52 after early termination.
corrections.basis: ClinicalTrials.gov results section for NCT06097260, retrieved 2026-09-03. The Phase 2 search used PubMed only and no peer-reviewed publication of these results was identified, so a registry-results check was required to find them.
corrections.effect: Landscape verdict changed Uncertain->Harm outweighs benefit; negative-results register row reclassified to the harm domain; new map statement M2.15; bexotegrast removed from M6.11; candidate P27 rejected as superseded by its own trial. Adds a methodological limitation to Phase 2: PubMed-only searching misses registry-posted results.

GALACTIC-1 (NCT03832946, n=172, quadruple-masked, 128 sites, completed) posts an annual FVC decline of -316.60 mL/year (95% CI -394.86 to -238.35) on GB0139 3 mg versus -127.41 mL/year (95% CI -221.12 to -33.71) on placebo, with respiratory hospitalisations 17 of 102 versus 5 of 70 and SGRQ change +4.201 versus -4.77. No between-arm test is posted, so the unfavourable direction is recorded without a harm verdict (conflicts register X12).

Orvepitant (NCT05185089, n=80 crossover): difference from placebo 0.00 (95% CI -0.62 to 0.63, p=0.989) at 10 mg and -0.58 (95% CI -1.16 to 0.01, p=0.054) at 30 mg. An IPF-specific triple-masked randomised monotherapy trial exists (NCT01969409, n=58): it met its autoantibody-titre primary endpoint (177 versus 288) and showed no benefit on FVC (2.5 versus 2.6 L), absolute survival (93% versus 93%) or transplant-free survival (90% versus 89%), with 12 versus 6 hospital admissions and 9 of 30 versus 5 of 28 serious adverse events. Bardoxolone methyl's only posted trial (LARIAT, NCT02036970) studied pulmonary hypertension with a 6-minute-walk primary endpoint (difference -1.74 m, 95% CI -16.22 to 12.74, p=0.8133) and inhaled treprostinil's posted trial enrolled ILD with pulmonary hypertension; both are labelled indirect. corrections.correction: The gap is now quantified from English-indexed systematic reviews that pooled Chinese-database trials: 63 randomised trials of Chinese medicine injections (PMID 35881610), 20 trials in 1363 patients across four injection products (PMID 36451506), 23 trials in 1390 patients of qi-supplementing and blood-activating herbs (PMID 35245333), 11 trials in 981 patients of external TCM treatment (PMID 41088620), a Chinese-herb-versus-N-acetylcysteine comparison in 733 patients (PMID 31312224), and an overview of reviews covering 15550 participants (PMID 37235494). Not one Chinese medicine injection product appears in the landscape, and the herbal-versus-N-acetylcysteine comparison is absent from the record. These reviews are secondary sources and their own quality statements are cautionary (limited number and quality of included studies), so no verdict is assigned to any of this evidence here.
corrections.basis: PubMed searches for Chinese herbal medicine, TCM injections, acupuncture and exercise interventions in IPF; abstracts of the six reviews listed; register ipf_phase6_chinese_language_coverage.csv. ClinicalTrials.gov mirror not applicable - these trials are registered in ChiCTR or unregistered.

corrections.claim_corrected: Kangxian Huanji Granule (PMID 37993378) was graded from a partial abstract, with the trial design not established.
corrections.correction: The full structured abstract is retrieved: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled exploratory trial, n=80, 10 g twice daily for 4 weeks added to conventional treatment in acute exacerbation of IPF, followed 12 weeks, registered as ChiCTR1900026289. Co-primary endpoints were treatment failure and all-cause mortality: treatment failure at 4 weeks RR 0.22 (95% CI 0.051-0.965, P=0.023); all-cause mortality at 16 weeks RR 0.75 (95% CI 0.179-3.138, P>0.999); acute exacerbation rate RR 0.69 (95% CI 0.334-1.434, P=0.317); length of hospitalisation -3.30 days (95% CI -6.300 to -0.300, P=0.032); mMRC -0.67 (95% CI -0.89 to -0.44, P<0.001) and SGRQ-I -10.36 (95% CI -16.483 to -4.228, P=0.001) at 4 weeks.
corrections.basis: Publisher abstract for doi 10.1016/j.joim.2023.11.003 retrieved via DOI resolution; full text remains closed access with no open-access or PubMed Central copy.
corrections.effect: Candidate P17 stays held at verification (screen S5): the design is now known but the full text, the ChiCTR record and any independent replication are still unavailable. The verdict remains Uncertain; the mortality endpoint is null and only the treatment-failure endpoint is positive, so the trial is not evidence of a survival effect.

corrections.claim_corrected: Full text of PMID 26331942 (TOLLIP x N-acetylcysteine interaction) was recorded as unobtainable.
corrections.correction: The PubMed Central deposit was retrieved but contains front matter and the abstract only (the article is closed access with no body text). The record's quoted values are now confirmed against the primary abstract: interaction P=0.001 for rs3750920; composite-endpoint hazard ratio 0.14 (95% CI 0.02-0.83, P=0.03) in TT patients and 3.23 (95% CI 0.79-13.16, P=0.10) in CC patients, with replication in an independent cohort and an explicit author call for a genotype-stratified prospective trial before any off-label recommendation.
corrections.basis: PubMed Central deposit for doi 10.1164/rccm.201505-1010OC (4.5 kB, abstract only); PubMed abstract.
corrections.effect: Candidate P10 stays unpromoted, but its reason changes: the numbers are verified, while the genotype subgroup sizes, whether the interaction was prespecified, and the replication cohort's composition remain unverifiable without publisher access. The genotype-stratified trial the authors asked for exists and is complete but unreported (PRECISIONS, action A1), so the smallest next step is retrieval, not a new trial.

corrections.claim_corrected: Landscape tallies of 281 rows, 278 distinct interventions and 194 'Poorly studied' rows, recorded in corrections C31 and C33.

Two entities were added by action A3 (SRN001 amphiregulin siRNA, PMID 42052104; an AI-discovered TNIK inhibitor, PMID 38459338), both phase 1 safety and pharmacokinetics only. One further duplicate name string was found ('Baduanjin exercise' as a case variant), and 'daoyin technique' is flagged as a probable but unverified duplicate of 'Pulmonary Daoyin'.

corrections.effect: Supersedes the counts in C31 and C33. Action A3 also established that better searching recovers very little: of 110 completed trials with no retrievable results, only 7 had any indexed publication and none of those reported the missing primary clinical outcome, so the deficit is genuine non-reporting rather than a search failure.

actions.subject: PRECISIONS (NCT04300920)
actions.detail: Genotype-stratified phase 3 of N-acetylcysteine in TOLLIP rs3750920 TT patients; primary completion 2026-03-02, no results posted at 2026-09-03. Request or await results; this is the direct test of the record's only surviving subgroup hypothesis.
