actions.phase6_detail: Rechecked ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-09-03: NCT04300920 is COMPLETED with actual primary completion and completion dates of 2026-03-02, hasResults false, no results section. PubMed holds only the design and rationale paper (PMID 36514019). This is the single most consequential pending result in the record: it is the genotype-stratified prospective trial that PMID 26331942 asked for and it determines the fate of candidate P10. Smallest next step: recheck the registry after the 12-month reporting deadline (2027-03-02), and in the interim watch conference abstracts and contact the coordinating centre for a reporting timeline. Nothing about N-acetylcysteine in TOLLIP rs3750920 TT patients should be restated until then.

actions.subject: closed-access key results
actions.detail: Full text of PMID 26331942 (TOLLIP x N-acetylcysteine interaction) and of the Kangxian Huanji granule trial (PMID 37993378) could not be obtained. Both are marked verification-incomplete and neither can be promoted until read.
actions.phase6_detail: PMID 26331942: the PubMed Central deposit was retrieved but holds front matter and abstract only (closed access, no body). The record's quoted interaction P=0.001 and hazard ratios 0.14 (0.02-0.83) and 3.23 (0.79-13.16) are confirmed against the primary abstract; genotype subgroup sizes, prespecification and the replication cohort remain unverified (correction C37). PMID 37993378 (Kangxian Huanji Granule): no open-access or PubMed Central copy exists, but the full structured abstract was retrieved, establishing a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled design in 80 patients with co-primary endpoints and all secondary effect estimates (correction C36). Smallest next step for both: institutional or publisher access, or an author request; for the granule trial also the ChiCTR1900026289 registration record.

actions.subject: 110 completed trials without retrievable results
actions.detail: 97 of them past the reporting window. Largest single addition available to this record. Not evidence of promise.
actions.phase6_detail: For each of the 110 completed trials with no retrievable results, PubMed was searched on the registry identifier. Only 7 returned any indexed publication, and none reported the missing primary clinical outcome: PRECISIONS (design paper), one pre-completion report, one methodological paper, and four safety, pharmacokinetic or preclinical papers. Two entities were added to the landscape from these (SRN001, PMID 42052104; TNIK inhibitor, PMID 38459338), both phase 1 only. Register ipf_phase6_missing_results_retrieval.csv; map row M5.15; correction C38. The deficit is genuine non-reporting, not a search failure.

actions.subject: Chinese-language databases
actions.detail: CNKI, VIP, Wanfang and SinoMed were not searchable from this environment; the traditional-medicine screen therefore rests on English-indexed records only.
actions.phase6_outcome: partially completed - direct database access blocked
actions.phase6_detail: ChiCTR and the WHO ICTRP portal were both requested and granted at the network level. ICTRP returns 403 from its own gateway for non-browser clients, and the ChiCTR search interface requires an encrypted, bot-protected browser session; neither was circumvented. CNKI, Wanfang, VIP and SinoMed remain inaccessible and are subscription-gated. What was executed instead: English-indexed systematic reviews that had searched those databases were used to quantify the missing literature - at least 63 randomised trials of Chinese medicine injections and several further pools totalling thousands of participants, with no injection product present in the landscape (correction C35, register ipf_phase6_chinese_language_coverage.csv, map row M5.14). This measures the size of the gap; it does not close it and assigns no verdict.

actions.subject: registry-results sweep of the full landscape
actions.detail: NEW Phase 4 finding: the Phase 2 search used PubMed only, and the bexotegrast harm result (C23) existed solely as a ClinicalTrials.gov results posting. A results-section check was run in Phase 4 for the 22 candidate subjects only; the remaining landscape entities have not been checked for posted-but-unpublished results.
actions.phase6_detail: Fetched the posted-results sections of all 116 IPF trials with results on ClinicalTrials.gov and matched them to the 281 landscape rows. 12 entities were reclassified (4 Failed, 8 Uncertain), 3 duplicate rows were merged, 4 entities were relabelled out-of-scope or indirect, 1 stopping reason was reclassified, and 9 entities were confirmed unchanged with a curation note. Two of the misses (gefapixant, tanzisertib) were published papers the Phase 2 search did not reach; the rest are unpublished registry postings. Corrections C24-C34; register ipf_phase6_registry_results_sweep.csv.

actions.subject: co-trimoxazole adherence
actions.detail: Adherence-stratified re-analysis of EME-TIPAC, acknowledging confounding by health status in open-label per-protocol comparisons.
actions.phase6_outcome: not executable within this record - individual participant data required
actions.phase6_detail: EME-TIPAC (PMID 33289822) is a double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 342 patients across 39 UK centres; 283 of 342 (83%) completed, and the primary endpoint hazard ratio was 1.2 (95% CI 0.9-1.6). No adherence-stratified or per-protocol re-analysis is published, and none of the trial's 15 secondary outcomes addresses adherence. The independent CleanUP-IPF trial (PMID 33974018) is also null, with an adjusted HR of 1.15 (95% CI 0.68-1.95) in its co-trimoxazole stratum. An adherence-stratified analysis cannot be done from published summaries: it requires individual participant dosing records. Smallest next step: request the EME-TIPAC dataset from the trial team and run a prespecified analysis using instrumental-variable or inverse-probability-weighted per-protocol methods, since a naive per-protocol comparison in an open-adherence setting is confounded by health status. Priority is low: two independent randomised trials are null, so the analysis would be testing whether a null was caused by non-adherence, not testing a positive signal.

actions.subject: corticosteroid harm magnitude
actions.detail: Quantify mortality association in existing cohorts with explicit handling of confounding by indication.
actions.phase6_outcome: completed - answered by existing synthesis; no new pooling warranted
actions.phase6_detail: The question is answered as far as existing data allow, and the answer is that the magnitude is not established. A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis (10 observational studies, 1639 patients with fibrotic ILD) found an uncertain effect of corticosteroids on mortality (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.85-1.25) and, in IPF specifically, an uncertain effect on FVC decline (mean difference -3.80% predicted, 95% CI -8.94 to 1.34), both very low certainty (PMID 38160015). In acute exacerbation the cohorts disagree in an interpretable way: no association with in-hospital mortality but worse overall survival in one propensity-weighted cohort (PMID 31846126), no advantage for pulse over non-pulse dosing (PMID 38087838), and better survival with early dose tapering (PMID 36289512). Re-pooling the same 10 observational studies would reproduce an existing analysis, so no new meta-analysis was performed. Map row M3.18. Smallest next step: a target-trial emulation in a prospective registry with time-varying corticosteroid exposure and explicit handling of confounding by indication, which requires registry data access rather than published summaries.

actions.subject: FVC-to-survival surrogacy
actions.detail: Trial-level or individual-participant meta-analysis; begin with a check of whether published meta-analyses already answer it.
actions.phase6_outcome: partially completed - the published literature answers a different question
actions.phase6_detail: The action's own first step was executed. Two primary sources address FVC and mortality: pooled nintedanib trial data (n=2583) show that a faster rate of FVC decline and a lower current FVC each predict death over 52 weeks (HR 1.79, 95% CI 1.57-2.03 and HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.17-1.32 per 5-percentage-point decrease; PMID 37646126), and a prospective registry shows adjusted 1.8-, 2.3- and 2.7-fold increases in death or transplantation after declines of at least 2%, 5% and 10% predicted (PMID 40020995). Both are patient-level prognostic analyses. Neither addresses treatment-effect surrogacy - whether a drug's effect on FVC predicts its effect on survival - which is the question this record depends on. That analysis was not attempted here: it requires paired FVC and mortality treatment effects extracted and verified trial by trial from primary reports, and individual IPF trials are underpowered for mortality. Map row M5.16. Smallest next step: assemble the trial-level dataset from primary publications and registry postings, then seek pooled individual participant data from sponsors before any surrogacy claim is made or relied upon.

actions.subject: recovery and reversal endpoints
actions.detail: No endpoint in the record measures recovery of lost lung function or reversal of established fibrosis.
actions.phase6_outcome: completed - endpoint set specified, none validated
actions.phase6_detail: Five candidate endpoints were specified for the dimensions the record cannot currently measure (reversal of established fibrosis, recovery of lost lung function, gas-transfer recovery, durable benefit after an exacerbation, and anchored functional recovery), each with a measurement approach, the existing validation evidence, feasibility, and the smallest validation step. Every one of the five smallest steps is a re-analysis of existing images or datasets, not a new trial. Register ipf_phase6_recovery_endpoints.csv. None of these endpoints is validated, and specifying them does not create evidence that recovery or reversal is achievable in IPF.

actions.subject: STRIVE-IPF (NCT03286556) analysis and publication
actions.detail: The largest single positive randomised signal in the record - six-month survival 44% versus 7% after acute exacerbation - exists only as a registry posting with no statistical analysis, no baseline severity data and no results paper (only design paper PMID 38509495). Smallest next step: request from the sponsor and investigators the statistical analysis plan, the baseline lung-function and oxygen-requirement table, the CONSORT flow reconciling 82 enrolled with 33 versus 18 analysed, and the primary survival analysis.
actions.phase6_detail: Opened by action A5. Not executable inside this record - requires contact with the trial team or a sponsor results publication.

actions.subject: N115 sodium pyruvate nasal spray (NCT06037408) protocol and publication
actions.detail: A single-site randomised posting claims a -57 percentage-point difference in daily cough episodes with a simultaneous 28% rise in the FEV1/FVC ratio and zero adverse events in 50 IPF patients. Smallest next step: obtain the protocol, the cough-measurement method and the analysis plan, and check whether any peer-reviewed report exists.

actions.subject: Chinese-language randomised IPF literature
actions.detail: Smallest next step, requiring a person or an institutional subscription rather than this environment: (1) retrieve ChiCTR1900026289 and any other ChiCTR IPF registrations by manual lookup; (2) run a Chinese-language search of CNKI, Wanfang, VIP and SinoMed for randomised trials of Chinese medicine injections and herbal formulas in IPF; (3) extract the individual trials pooled by PMID 35881610, 36451506 and 35245333 from those reviews' reference lists and grade them individually against this record's tiers. Priority is the injection class, which is wholly absent from the landscape despite dozens of randomised trials.
actions.phase6_detail: Opened by action A4 after direct database access failed.

limitations.detail: PubMed-only searching missed a randomised trial (C12), an adequately powered trial (C13), two sildenafil sources (C14), a phase 2b null (C15) and a registry-only harm result (C23). Eleven of the twelve Phase 4 corrections are retrieval artefacts of the Phase 2 search, not changes of judgement about the same evidence.
The registry-results check was run for the 22 candidate subjects, not for all 281 landscape entities (action A5).
Two candidate key results could not be verified against primary full text (P10, P17) and are recorded as held, not rejected and not promoted.
No pooling or re-estimation was performed in Phase 4; all figures are quoted from their source reports.

limitations.scope: one source with an internal inconsistency
limitations.detail: The endurance-time interval in PMID 37012071 as printed does not contain its own point estimate; reproduced verbatim and flagged, full text not obtained.

limitations.scope: Phase 2 search strategy; Phase 6 action A5
limitations.detail: Entity-level literature searching in Phase 2 was PubMed-only and did not include a registry posted-results check, so trials that were completed but unpublished were graded as absent evidence. Action A5 corrected this for the whole landscape, but two consequences remain: (i) nine entities now rest on registry postings whose between-arm analyses the sponsor never posted, which can be described and not weighed; (ii) the sweep covers ClinicalTrials.gov only - EudraCT, jRCT, ChiCTR and other national registries were not swept, so the same class of miss may persist for trials registered elsewhere.

limitations.scope: Phase 2 traditional-medicine screen; Phase 6 action A4
limitations.detail: The record's coverage of traditional Chinese medicine rests on English-indexed sources. Direct access to CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, SinoMed, ChiCTR and the WHO ICTRP portal was not achieved from this environment (ICTRP's gateway refuses non-browser clients; ChiCTR's search requires an encrypted browser session; the Chinese bibliographic databases are subscription-gated). Action A4 quantified the resulting gap from secondary reviews: at least 63 randomised trials of Chinese medicine injections and several further pools totalling thousands of participants sit outside the record, and no injection product appears in the landscape. Any statement this record makes about traditional Chinese medicine in IPF is therefore made on a demonstrably partial sample, and the direction of the missing evidence is unknown.

unmet_needs.unmet_need: No intervention has been shown to recover lost lung function in humans; the best active arm still declines.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: Least-declining active arm reported: -21.5 mL/26 wk (ELEVATE-IPF, PMID 42085224). All phase 3 positive arms decline -43.3 to -138.6 mL/52 wk.

unmet_needs.unmet_need: Reversal of established fibrosis has never been demonstrated, measured or defined as a human endpoint.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: No human trial endpoint for reversal in retrieved evidence; quantitative HRCT has no accepted MCID and is not a registration endpoint.
unmet_needs.status: Gap; preclinical reports do not license human claims (L2)

unmet_needs.unmet_need: No randomised evidence that any drug prolongs survival in IPF.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: Only RCT with mortality as primary endpoint was negative (INSPIRE, HR 1.15, 95% CI 0.77-1.71). Survival signals are observational: pooled RR 0.55 (0.45-0.66, I2=82%), registry HR 0.56 (0.34-0.92), causal-inference HR 0.53 (0.28-1.03).
unmet_needs.status: Structurally unaddressed: mortality trials in mild-to-moderate IPF judged of prohibitive size, duration and cost (PMID 24476390)

unmet_needs.unmet_need: No intervention has shown a dyspnoea or quality-of-life benefit exceeding the relevant MCID in a pivotal IPF trial.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: INSTAGE SGRQ -1.28 vs -0.36 (null, PMID 30220235); no positive HRQoL pivotal result retrieved.
unmet_needs.status: Unaddressed; complicated by contested MCID thresholds

unmet_needs.unmet_need: Cough has one small, short randomised positive result and no durable treatment.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: PACIFY COUGH: -39.4% awake cough frequency at day 14, n=44 (PMID 38237620); omeprazole pilot -39.1% with CI crossing null (PMID 30610155).
unmet_needs.status: Partially addressed at 14 days; durability, generalisability and MCID all unknown

unmet_needs.unmet_need: No adequately powered randomised evidence for preventing or treating acute exacerbations; the one randomised treatment attempt signalled harm.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: Pooled RR 0.63 (0.53-0.76) is predominantly observational (PMID 34217681); TETON-1/-2 exacerbation endpoints hierarchy-stopped; EXAFIP cyclophosphamide 3-month mortality 45% vs 31% (PMID 34506761).
unmet_needs.status: Unaddressed; in-hospital mortality after an exacerbation remains ~29.5% (PMID 35614114)

unmet_needs.unmet_need: Durability of antifibrotic effect beyond 52 weeks has never been randomised.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: Every pivotal trial for an approved or recently positive agent is <=52 weeks.
unmet_needs.status: Unaddressed; extensions and real-world cohorts are not randomised comparisons

unmet_needs.unmet_need: The field's own endpoint methodology is unresolved: incompatible FVC metrics, direction-dependent and disputed MCIDs, and no retrieved trial-level surrogacy validation.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: Four distinct FVC metrics across pivotal trials with ~3-fold variation in placebo-arm decline; K-BILD MID estimates differ 2-3 fold (PMID 23867809 vs 32316976); MCIDs re-estimated substantially higher by anchor-only methods (PMID 34671666); two literature searches for trial-level FVC-mortality surrogacy returned no validation study.
unmet_needs.status: Unaddressed; this is a precondition for interpreting every other dimension

unmet_needs.unmet_need: The randomised evidence base is concentrated in mild-to-moderate physiologic impairment; severe disease is under-represented.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: Mortality-rate analysis and MCID derivation both specify mild-to-moderate impairment (PMID 24476390; PMID 42548365); PACIFY COUGH mean FVC 82 %pred.
unmet_needs.status: Unaddressed; effect estimates and MCIDs may not transfer across severity strata

unmet_needs.unmet_need: Results of a large fraction of completed IPF trials cannot be found.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: Of 239 completed interventional IPF studies, 90 have posted results, 39 have a post-completion linked publication (primary outcome unverified) and 110 have neither; 97 of those (4,182 participants) completed more than 12 months ago. 21 of the 97 were phase 2 or 3.

unmet_needs.unmet_need: No validated predictive biomarker identifies who benefits from which treatment; the one prospective genotype-selected trial has not reported.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: TOLLIP rs3750920 x NAC interaction is retrospective (PMID 26331942); PRECISIONS (NCT04300920, n=202) completed 2026-03-02 with no results posted and only a design paper indexed (PMID 36514019).
unmet_needs.status: Open; PRECISIONS is within its 12-month reporting window as of 2026-09-02 (see corrections log)

unmet_needs.unmet_need: Non-pharmacological and supportive care evidence is largely ILD-wide rather than IPF-specific.
unmet_needs.evidence_basis: Cochrane pulmonary rehabilitation review covers interstitial lung disease broadly (PMID 34559419); no IPF-specific randomised oxygen trial was identified by this search.
unmet_needs.status: Open; under L1 such evidence enters only as labelled indirect evidence

open_questions.question: Is any part of established fibrosis reversible in humans?
open_questions.current_evidence: No intervention has shown recovery of lost FVC in any completed IPF RCT; best active arms still decline (fig 1b). Reversal has only been reported preclinically.
open_questions.smallest_useful_next_step: Re-analysis of individual-participant data from completed phase 3 trials for any subgroup with sustained positive FVC slope; quantitative HRCT re-reads of existing trial imaging.

open_questions.question: Does antifibrotic therapy prolong survival, and by how much?
open_questions.current_evidence: No individual RCT was powered for mortality (ASCEND all-cause death P=0.10; a mortality trial would need ~508 events for 90% power to detect 25% reduction). Meta-analysis reports pooled RR 0.55 (0.45-0.66) but pools heterogeneous trials; real-world cohorts are confounded by treatment selection.
open_questions.smallest_useful_next_step: Individual-participant-data meta-analysis of all phase 3 antifibrotic trials with consistent mortality adjudication; target-trial emulation in national registries.

open_questions.question: Does the TOLLIP rs3750920 genotype identify NAC responders?
open_questions.current_evidence: A retrospective pharmacogenomic interaction (PANTHER) motivated the prospective PRECISIONS trial (NCT04300920, n=202), which is registered as completed with no results posted and no primary publication indexed as of 2026-09-02.
open_questions.smallest_useful_next_step: Retrieval of PRECISIONS results from the sponsor/consortium; if unavailable, formal results-request and registry non-compliance documentation.

open_questions.question: Is immunosuppression harmful in all IPF patients or only in a telomere-defined subgroup?
open_questions.current_evidence: Triple therapy caused excess death and hospitalisation in PANTHER; observational work reports interaction with short telomere length; no prospective test exists.
open_questions.smallest_useful_next_step: Genotype- and telomere-stratified re-analysis of PANTHER and cohort data; no new exposure trial without a strong safety rationale.

open_questions.question: Do the two approved antifibrotics plus a new-mechanism agent add up?
open_questions.current_evidence: Nerandomilast was tested on a 77.7% background-antifibrotic population and treprostinil trials allowed background therapy, but no trial has randomised the addition of a second agent versus switching or versus maximal single therapy.
open_questions.smallest_useful_next_step: Registry-based comparative-effectiveness analysis of add-on versus switch in routine care; then a pragmatic randomised add-on strategy trial.

open_questions.question: Why did positive phase 2 signals fail in phase 3 so consistently?
open_questions.current_evidence: Pentraxin-2 (positive phase 2 FVC and 6MWD) failed phase 3 futility; pamrevlumab, ziritaxestat and others repeated the pattern. Placebo-arm decline varied roughly 3-fold across trials (112 to 330 mL), which alone can create or erase an apparent effect.
open_questions.smallest_useful_next_step: Cross-trial analysis of placebo-arm decline versus enrolment criteria and calendar year; quantification of how much phase 2 to phase 3 attrition is explained by control-arm drift and endpoint choice.

open_questions.question: Is there any evidence-based treatment for acute exacerbation of IPF?
open_questions.current_evidence: Cyclophosphamide showed a non-significant excess of 3-month mortality (45% vs 31%); high-dose corticosteroids are standard of care but supported only by observational data with inconsistent and sometimes adverse signals in IPF.
open_questions.smallest_useful_next_step: Systematic retrieval of all AE-IPF interventional data including unpublished; target-trial emulation of steroid dose strategies in hospital datasets.

open_questions.question: Can cough and dyspnoea be treated without accelerating harm?
open_questions.current_evidence: Low-dose morphine reduced objective cough frequency (21.6 to 12.8/h vs 21.5 to 20.6/h) with adverse events 40% vs 14%; omeprazole cough effect CI crossed the null; the two approved antifibrotics and treprostinil all increase cough or gastrointestinal burden.
open_questions.smallest_useful_next_step: Larger replication of the opioid cough result with harm surveillance; pooled patient-reported-outcome analysis across existing phase 3 datasets.

open_questions.question: Does the large Chinese-language TCM trial base contain any testable signal?
open_questions.current_evidence: Evidence mapping identified 323 clinical studies including 295 RCTs and 28 meta-analyses, but the RCTs were generally low quality with small samples, short courses, non-standardised syndrome definitions and undifferentiated primary/secondary outcomes.
open_questions.smallest_useful_next_step: Screen the 295 RCTs for any with objective FVC/DLCO endpoints, adequate duration and low risk of bias; assess whether any single formula has replicated results worth independent testing.

open_questions.question: Is FVC change at 52 weeks an adequate basis for the whole field?
open_questions.current_evidence: Every approved and near-approved agent rests on a millilitre-scale FVC difference; trials used at least four different FVC metrics (annual rate, absolute change, median change, categorical decline), and secondary endpoints (exacerbation, mortality, symptoms) were repeatedly non-significant or hierarchy-stopped.
open_questions.smallest_useful_next_step: Validation study of the FVC-to-outcome mapping using pooled trial data; explicit minimal clinically important difference work anchored to survival and patient-reported outcomes.

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: Largest 52-week between-group FVC difference in a phase 3 IPF trial: 130.1 mL (95% CI 82.2-178.1), inhaled treprostinil vs placebo, median change -43.3 vs -196.2 mL
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: Every active arm of every positive trial still declines. Across positive phase 3 arms the active-arm change ranges from -43.3 to -138.6 mL/52 wk.
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: Metrics are not interchangeable: TETON reports median change, INPULSIS annual rate, FIBRONEER absolute change; placebo-arm decline ranges from -136.4 to -239.9 mL, so mL differences cannot be ranked across trials (L3).

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: 47.9% relative reduction in the proportion of patients with >=10 point FVC%pred decline or death at 52 weeks (pirfenidone vs placebo)
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: No trial has shown that progression can be prevented outright; the residual progression rate in treated arms remains substantial.
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: Categorical and continuous FVC endpoints are not interchangeable (E3).

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: Least-declining active arm reported: -21.5 mL over 26 weeks (deupirfenidone 825 mg, frequentist adjusted mean change)
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: No completed IPF RCT arm has reported a sustained positive change in FVC. Recovery of lost function has never been demonstrated in humans.
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: A near-zero slope over 26 weeks is not recovery and is not durable evidence; the trial's own verdict class is Uncertain.

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: None. No human trial endpoint measures reversal (E15).
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: Everything. There is no validated measure, no trial precedent and no regulatory pathway.
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: Preclinical reversal reports do not license any human claim (L2).

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: Pooled RR 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, I2=0%) for acute exacerbation with antifibrotic therapy
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: No adequately powered randomised demonstration of acute-exacerbation reduction; TETON-1/-2 exacerbation endpoints were hierarchy-stopped, i.e. not formally tested (L3).
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: Incidence and prognosis both shifted with the 2016 definition change (E10), so pooled historical estimates mix definitions.

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: Highest documented placebo-adjusted reduction in objective cough frequency: 60.2% relative reduction (31.5 to 11.9 coughs/h; P<.001) with nalbuphine ER 108 mg vs 16.9% with placebo at week 6; earlier crossover trial reported a 50.8 percentage-point placebo-adjusted change at day 21. Low-dose morphine gave 39.4% (95% CI -54.4 to -19.4; p=0.0005) at day 14.
therapeutic_ceiling.evidence_tier: RCT (phase 2b dose-ranging, 6 weeks) + RCT (crossover) + RCT (small crossover)
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: Durability beyond 6 weeks, independent (non-sponsor) replication, the phase 3 result, and any effect on disease course. Opioid-class tolerability is the trade-off: nausea, fatigue, constipation and dizziness exceeded placebo in the crossover trial.
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: Symptom domain only; licenses no statement about fibrosis, lung function or progression (E9). Updated in C11.

therapeutic_ceiling.dimension: Symptoms - dyspnoea / health-related quality of life
therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: No intervention has shown an HRQoL or dyspnoea difference exceeding the relevant MCID in a pivotal IPF trial in retrieved evidence. INSTAGE (nintedanib+sildenafil) SGRQ difference -1.28 vs -0.36, null.
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: Any demonstrated improvement in how patients feel, as opposed to how fast a surrogate declines.
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: MCID thresholds themselves are contested (E6, E7).

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: No positive pivotal result. STEP-IPF primary endpoint (>=20% 6MWD improvement) 10% vs 7%, not significant.
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: A demonstrated improvement in exercise capacity from any disease-directed drug.
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: Pulmonary rehabilitation evidence is separate and is not disease-directed therapy.

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: No randomised evidence of a survival benefit for any drug. Best available: pooled RR 0.55 (95% CI 0.45-0.66, I2=82%) for all-cause mortality with antifibrotics; registry HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.34-0.92); causal-inference HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.28-1.03, p=0.060).
therapeutic_ceiling.evidence_tier: Meta-analysis of mostly observational data; registry; causal-inference cohort
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: A randomised mortality demonstration. Trial-level surrogacy of FVC for mortality was not established in any source retrieved by this Phase 1 search.
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: All-cause-mortality trials in mild-to-moderate IPF were judged of prohibitive size, duration and cost (PMID 24476390), which is why this gap persists; the only RCT with mortality as primary endpoint was negative (INSPIRE HR 1.15, 95% CI 0.77-1.71).

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: Randomised comparison is limited to ~52 weeks for every currently approved or recently positive agent.
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: Randomised evidence beyond one year; whether the slope difference is maintained, widens or attenuates.
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: Open-label extension and real-world cohorts are not randomised comparisons.

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: Lung transplantation: 5-year survival 55.2% in the most recent era analysed, up from 51.9% (p=0.02); adjusted HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.76-0.91) for the later era
therapeutic_ceiling.what_remains_unachieved: Transplantation is limited by candidacy, organ supply and age; it replaces the lung rather than treating the disease. Bilateral vs single choice trades short-term for long-term risk (PMID 19949142).
therapeutic_ceiling.caveat: No randomised comparison of transplantation against medical therapy exists or is feasible.

therapeutic_ceiling.best_documented_result: None reported in any retrieved human evidence.

endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: annual rate (mL/yr); change to week 52; slope
endpoint_taxonomy.threshold_or_mcid: No MCID defined in mL; MCID is defined in % (see E2/E3)
endpoint_taxonomy.licenses: A between-group difference in mean decline over the trial period
endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: 'preserves lung function', 'stabilises', survival benefit, symptom benefit
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Used as the primary endpoint of most pivotal trials; not anchored to any patient-perceived change; placebo-arm decline differs ~3-fold across trials, so cross-trial comparison of mL differences is not valid
endpoint_taxonomy.evidence_level: Regulatory-accepted primary endpoint; no retrieved trial-level surrogate validation

endpoint_taxonomy.prognostic_anchor: 24-week FVC decline of 5-10% -> >2-fold higher 1-year mortality (P<0.001); 'marginal' decline HR 2.31 (95% CI 1.19-4.50)
endpoint_taxonomy.licenses: A clinically important difference only if the between-group difference reaches 2-6 %pred
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: MCID derived largely from death/hospitalisation and distribution-based anchors; single value may not apply across severity strata or follow-up durations (PMID 34671666)
endpoint_taxonomy.evidence_level: Anchor- and distribution-based MCID studies in trial cohorts

endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: relative vs absolute definition; >=10% vs >=5%; with/without death as competing event
endpoint_taxonomy.prognostic_anchor: Relative change maximises detection of >=10% decline without sacrificing prognostic accuracy; absolute change more predictive at the >=5% level; all thresholds of FVC and DLCO decline associated with death or transplant (PMID 40020995)
endpoint_taxonomy.licenses: Proportion of patients crossing a prognostically meaningful threshold
endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: Equivalence with the continuous FVC endpoint; pooling with mL differences
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Relative and absolute definitions are not interchangeable; choice changes both event rate and effect estimate

endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: absolute vs relative decline; >=10% and >=15% thresholds
endpoint_taxonomy.threshold_or_mcid: No IPF-specific MCID retrieved; >=10% decline used as prognostic threshold
endpoint_taxonomy.prognostic_anchor: DLCO decline >=10% predicted mortality in a real-world pirfenidone cohort; for DLCO (unlike FVC) risk increase was generally greater for relative than absolute thresholds (PMID 40020995)
endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: Substitution for FVC endpoints; symptom or survival claims
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Higher measurement variability than FVC; frequently a secondary or exploratory endpoint, so nulls are often underpowered rather than informative

endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: change at 24/52 weeks; distance vs desaturation
endpoint_taxonomy.prognostic_anchor: 24-week decline >50 m -> HR 4.27 (95% CI 2.57-7.10) for 1-year death
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Anchor-only re-estimation gives considerably higher MCID values than the original estimates (PMID 34671666); ceiling/floor effects by severity

endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: SGRQ vs IPF-specific SGRQ-I; improvement vs deterioration
endpoint_taxonomy.prognostic_anchor: Not a validated prognostic anchor for mortality in retrieved evidence
endpoint_taxonomy.licenses: Patient-reported health-status change on the measured domain
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: MCID differs by direction of change, so a symmetric threshold misclassifies deterioration; not interchangeable with K-BILD

endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: Comparison against SGRQ thresholds; disease modification
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Published MID estimates differ by a factor of ~2-3 depending on method and direction; a trial can be 'positive' or 'null' depending on which is adopted

endpoint_taxonomy.threshold_or_mcid: MCID for worsening 4-6, point estimate 6 (mild/moderate impairment)
endpoint_taxonomy.prognostic_anchor: Anchored to FVC (6), 6MWD (4.3) and SGRQ-A (5.8) cut points
endpoint_taxonomy.licenses: Patient-reported dyspnoea change in mild-to-moderate disease
endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: Extrapolation to severe disease; disease modification
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Derived in mild/moderate impairment only; MCID for improvement not established in retrieved evidence

endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: objective digital cough monitoring vs VAS vs Leicester Cough Questionnaire
endpoint_taxonomy.threshold_or_mcid: No IPF-specific MCID retrieved for objective cough frequency or VAS
endpoint_taxonomy.prognostic_anchor: None; cough is not a prognostic endpoint
endpoint_taxonomy.licenses: Symptom effect only, over the measured interval (14 days in PACIFY COUGH)
endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: Any statement about fibrosis, lung function, or progression
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Short measurement windows; entry requires VAS >=30 mm so results do not generalise to unselected patients

endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: 2007 definition vs 2016 revised international working-group definition; 'acute respiratory deterioration' superset
endpoint_taxonomy.prognostic_anchor: In-hospital mortality after AE 29.5% under the revised definition; revised definition raised measured incidence ~20% and lowered in-hospital mortality ~10% relative to the old one (PMID 35614114)
endpoint_taxonomy.licenses: Change in the rate of a defined acute event, under the definition used
endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: Comparison across trials using different definitions; substitution for mortality
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Definition change alters both numerator and prognosis, so historical and modern rates are not comparable; incidence estimates vary widely (3-year 18.6%; PMID 39256473)
endpoint_taxonomy.evidence_level: Consensus definition + systematic review of cohorts

endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: all-cause vs respiratory; death or transplant composite
endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: Nothing weaker may substitute for it
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: In mild-to-moderate IPF the event rate is low enough that the size, duration and cost of an all-cause-mortality trial are 'substantial and likely prohibitive' (PMID 24476390); consequently no pivotal IPF trial is powered for mortality

endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: time to first vs rate; all-cause vs respiratory
endpoint_taxonomy.prognostic_anchor: Not separately validated in retrieved evidence
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Definitions vary; observational estimates can move in the opposite direction to mortality estimates in the same cohort (PMID 36997445)

endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: automated quantitative CT scores; visual semi-quantitative reads
endpoint_taxonomy.prognostic_anchor: Automated quantitative CT change predicts outcome longitudinally (PMID 31196945)
endpoint_taxonomy.licenses: Structural change of the measured feature
endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: Reversal of fibrosis; functional or survival benefit
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Not a registration endpoint; methods are not standardised across centres, so cross-study pooling is not possible

endpoint_taxonomy.measure: Progression-free survival / time to disease progression
endpoint_taxonomy.metric_variants: components differ by trial (FVC threshold, death, hospitalisation, 6MWD)
endpoint_taxonomy.licenses: Only the composite as defined in that trial
endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: Comparison across trials; interpretation as survival benefit
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: Component definitions are not standardised; a composite dominated by an FVC threshold inherits every problem of E3 while reading as a hard outcome

endpoint_taxonomy.dimension: Recovery of lost function / reversal of fibrosis
endpoint_taxonomy.licenses: Nothing; no IPF trial endpoint currently measures recovery of lost lung function
endpoint_taxonomy.does_not_license: Any claim of reversal from FVC-slope, imaging or preclinical data
endpoint_taxonomy.known_problems: This is the central endpoint gap: the outcome patients most want has no validated measure, no trial precedent and no regulatory pathway; sustained positive FVC slope has not been demonstrated in any completed IPF RCT arm

measurement_gaps.endpoint: Change in quantitative CT fibrosis extent (data-driven texture or e-Lung style automated scores)
measurement_gaps.why_needed: No endpoint in the record measures whether fibrosis regresses. FVC can rise for reasons unrelated to fibrosis (effort, weight, comorbid resolution) and cannot distinguish arrest from reversal.
measurement_gaps.approach: Paired quantitative CT at baseline and 12 months with a prespecified regression threshold defined as a decrease in fibrosis extent exceeding measurement error, established from same-day repeat scans.
measurement_gaps.existing_validation: Quantitative CT scores are associated with outcomes in fibrotic ILD cohorts (for example the e-Lung biomarker literature), but no published threshold for regression exists and no trial has used regression as an endpoint.
measurement_gaps.feasibility: High: uses scans already acquired in most trials and registries.
measurement_gaps.smallest_validation_step: Retrospective application to an existing trial or registry image set with same-day repeat scans, to estimate measurement error and the proportion of patients showing change beyond it. No new patient contact required.

measurement_gaps.endpoint: Sustained FVC improvement of at least 5% predicted maintained for at least 6 months
measurement_gaps.why_needed: Trials report mean change and categorical decline thresholds; a durable improvement category is almost never prespecified, so the record cannot say how often improvement occurs or whether any treatment increases it.
measurement_gaps.approach: Prespecified responder analysis requiring two consecutive measurements at least 6 months apart both above the baseline threshold, with sensitivity analysis for measurement variability.
measurement_gaps.existing_validation: Categorical decline thresholds are validated prognostically (PMID 40020995); the mirror-image improvement category has no comparable validation.
measurement_gaps.feasibility: High: computable from existing trial datasets without new measurement.
measurement_gaps.smallest_validation_step: Re-analysis of completed placebo-controlled trial datasets to estimate the background rate of sustained improvement under placebo and under active treatment. This is a data-request and re-analysis step, not a new trial.

measurement_gaps.endpoint: Time to sustained improvement in gas transfer (DLco) beyond measurement error
measurement_gaps.why_needed: DLco is usually a secondary endpoint reported as mean change; the record contains no intervention with evidence of DLco recovery, and it is unknown whether the absence reflects biology or measurement practice.
measurement_gaps.approach: Repeat-measurement error model from within-subject same-visit duplicates, then a time-to-event analysis of first sustained improvement above that error.
measurement_gaps.existing_validation: DLco decline thresholds are prognostically validated in registry data (PMID 40020995).
measurement_gaps.feasibility: Moderate: requires duplicate-measurement data, which few datasets retain.
measurement_gaps.smallest_validation_step: Estimate within-visit DLco reproducibility in one existing cohort with duplicate measurements before proposing the endpoint for any trial.

measurement_gaps.endpoint: Six-month survival free of acute exacerbation after a first exacerbation
measurement_gaps.dimension: durable benefit after an acute event
measurement_gaps.why_needed: The only positive randomised survival signal in the record (STRIVE-IPF) uses six-month survival after an exacerbation, and no comparable endpoint is standardised, so the signal cannot be compared with anything.
measurement_gaps.approach: Composite of survival and freedom from a further adjudicated exacerbation, with blinded adjudication against consensus exacerbation criteria.
measurement_gaps.existing_validation: Exacerbation criteria are consensus-defined but adjudication practice varies between trials; the composite itself is unvalidated.
measurement_gaps.feasibility: Moderate: needs adjudication infrastructure but no new measurement technology.
measurement_gaps.smallest_validation_step: Apply the composite retrospectively to the two registered exacerbation trials and to STRIVE-IPF's own data once the analysis is released (action A10), to establish event rates and adjudication agreement.

measurement_gaps.endpoint: Patient-reported functional recovery anchored to a measured activity threshold
measurement_gaps.dimension: symptoms and function, anchored rather than self-referential
measurement_gaps.why_needed: Symptom instruments in the record (SGRQ-I, K-BILD, cough scores) measure change in reported state but are not anchored to any measured capacity, so symptom improvement cannot be separated from expectation effects in unblinded studies, which is precisely the weakness of the record's open-label positive signals.
measurement_gaps.approach: Pair an instrument change with a concurrently measured objective anchor (actigraphy step count or a standardised walk test) and define recovery as improvement in both.
measurement_gaps.existing_validation: Both components are individually used in IPF trials; the paired definition is not validated.
measurement_gaps.feasibility: High: actigraphy and walk tests are already collected in many trials.
measurement_gaps.smallest_validation_step: Correlate existing paired instrument and actigraphy data in a completed trial or registry to determine whether an anchored definition is achievable at all.
